What’s new for the 2026 tax season

The One Big Beautiful Bill Act introduced significant changes to 1099 tax reporting. This article summarizes the key changes and how they may affect you.

1099-NEC and 1099-MISC reporting threshold

In 2026, The One Big Beautiful Bill Act raised the federal reporting threshold for 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC forms from 600 USD to 2,000 USD.

The 1099-K federal reporting threshold remains greater than 20,000 USD in total gross volume and 200 transactions.

Qualified tip reporting

Platforms and Marketplaces

Platforms can report qualified tips and associated occupation codes on behalf of their connected accounts. Two options are available depending on where you are in the filing process:

  • Before filing use the Tax Forms Editor: Adjust form totals to reflect qualified tips and associated occupation codes.
  • After filing use Corrections: Update tax year 2026 forms to include qualified tips and associated occupation codes.

Stripe Issued Tax Forms

Merchants receiving a Stripe-issued 1099-K tax form can self-certify their qualified tips prior to filing or as a correction after filing.

Stripe does not determine whether a tip is qualified for tax purposes. Platforms and form recipients should confirm the information reported on a form with a tax professional.

IRIS Portal

The IRS is retiring its legacy FIRE (Filing Information Returns Electronically) system and replacing it with IRIS (Information Returns Intake System) — a modernized, API-first intake platform. FIRE retirement is targeted for December 31, 2026, making IRIS the sole intake for information returns beginning with tax year 2026 filings (due in early 2027). Platforms using the Connect 1099 product should not experience many differences, though there are several new requirements and behavioral differences with IRIS.

Real-Time Submission Validation

Unlike FIRE, IRIS returns real-time validation results. Each submission can result in one of the following statuses:

  • Accepted — submission processed successfully
  • Accepted with Errors — submission accepted but some records contain errors
  • Partially Accepted — submission processed the transmission (accepted and rejected one or more submissions)
  • Rejected — the entire submission was rejected and must be corrected and resubmitted as an original

Issuer Phone Number Is Now Required

IRIS requires a valid Issuer Phone Number as part of the issuer/payer record. This field is mandatory. Platforms (issuers) that have not historically provided a phone number will need to provide one. This is a new data requirement that did not exist under FIRE.

Foreign Issuers Must Have an EIN

All issuers (payers) must have a US Employer Identification Number (EIN) or SSN that matches the IRS database. Foreign issuers without a US EIN cannot file through IRIS — submissions will be rejected with “Issuer EIN does not match IRS database.” Foreign issuers need to apply for an EIN via the IRS online EIN application. This was less strictly enforced under FIRE (filers without an EIN received a letter but the submission was not automatically rejected).

Where is my 1099-K tax form?

Stripe issues 1099-K forms to eligible accounts and makes them available in your Dashboard by January 31 for the prior tax year.

Find your 1099-K form

  • Go to the Documents page in your Dashboard.
  • Click the 1099-K PDF for the relevant tax year to download.

You need Administrator or Tax Analyst access to view and download tax forms from the Dashboard. Confirm your account role with your account owner if needed.

If you don’t see a 1099-K form

  • Before January 31: Your 1099-K form may not be available yet
  • After January 31: You may not be eligible for a 1099-K form. A 1099-K is only issued if your account met the IRS or state reporting thresholds for that tax year. If your account did not meet the threshold, Stripe does not issue a 1099-K for that year.

Corporate Card

Corporate Card PIN Support

Stripe Corporate Cards do not support PINs at this time, so you will not be asked to set one up. In the case that a merchant asks for a PIN when completing a purchase with your Stripe Corporate Card, we recommend asking them to process the transaction as a chip and signature card (rather than a chip and PIN).

Corporate Card: I want to cancel an authorized charge

Once a transaction has been authorized, we are unable to cancel the transaction. We recommend reaching out directly to the merchant to request a refund for the purchase if you need to cancel a charge on your Stripe Corporate Card.

Corporate Card: My transaction was canceled

When you make a purchase, a transaction is first authorized for the charge amount. This authorization step confirms to the merchant that you have the funds available to make the purchase. Authorized transactions will appear as “pending” in your Dashboard.

Once a charge is authorized, merchants have up to seven days to capture the funds in order to complete the transaction. If an authorization is captured, the transaction completes, and the “pending” status will be removed and replaced by a “required” status if a receipt upload is needed for the transaction, or nothing if no receipt is required.

If an authorization is not captured, the authorized funds will be released and the transaction will show as “canceled”. This can happen manually through merchant action (i.e. if you request a refund from the merchant immediately after making a purchase and the merchant releases the authorization), or automatically if the transaction is not captured within the seven days time.

Corporate Card: My transaction was declined

If you encounter an unexpected decline, we suggest you check your card settings for these common causes and troubleshooting tips. You should also receive an SMS with the reason for each declined transaction.

  • Credit limits: Transactions will not be authorized if they would bring your Stripe Corporate Card balance higher than your current credit limit.
    • You can make more frequent payments to free up additional credit for use during your statement cycle.
  • Frozen cards: When a Stripe Corporate Card is frozen, all subsequent purchase authorizations on that card will automatically be declined.
    • You can unfreeze a Stripe Corporate Card at any time through your Stripe Corporate Card dashboard.
  • Spending limits: The spending limit on the card has been reached and/or the transaction is in one of the blocked categories set for the card.
    • If you need these settings to be adjusted, please reach out to an administrator on your account.
  • Zip or CVC mismatch: The incorrect CVC or zip code information was provided during checkout.
    • You can confirm the CVC and ZIP in the Your Card section of the Dashboard, and retry the transaction by providing the correct zip code and cvc information.

A transaction showing a “canceled” status is not the same as a decline. A canceled transaction means that the transaction was authorized successfully but the funds were ultimately not captured. You can learn more about canceled transactions here:

Corporate Card: My transaction was canceled

Corporate Card: Naming virtual Corporate Cards

Virtual Stripe Corporate Cards are digital cards that give you the flexibility to make purchases online. They are not tied to specific cardholders. Instead, virtual Stripe Corporate Cards are tied to your Stripe Merchant account and can be set up for specific payments, like recurring subscriptions, and you can designate custom limits in real-time.

Because virtual cards aren’t tied to a specific cardholder, a common naming convention is to use [your Company Name] as a First name and [X_Service_Expense] as a Last name. An example of this is “Stripe Events” or “Stripe Office_Supplies”.

Please note that it is not currently possible to edit the name of a virtual Corporate Card once you’ve created it. If you need to rename a card, you will need to delete the current card and re-create a new one with the new name from your Dashboard.

Corporate Card: Pay Now option unavailable

You can pay your Corporate Card bill at any time for an amount up to your current balance by selecting the Pay Now option from your Dashboard.

If the Pay Now option is greyed out and unavailable for use, this is because you do not currently have a balance to be paid off. Transactions cannot be paid off while they are still pending, so the Pay Now button will only be available once transactions are confirmed and posted to your current statement balance.

Corporate Card: Pricing and Fees

The Stripe Corporate Card is free to use. There is no periodic interest because you pay your statement balance in full each month and there are no other fees associated with using the Stripe Corporate Card (e.g., no annual fees, no foreign transaction fees, no late payment fees, and no additional card or card replacement fees).

Additional Information

Corporate Card

Corporate Card: Understanding transaction statuses

Corporate Card transactions can have one of the following statuses:

  • A blank status means the transaction was successful, and has been posted to your statement with no further action needed.
  • Attached: This transaction was successful, but required a receipt upload. A receipt has successfully been attached to the transaction at this time, so no further action is needed.
  • Canceled: A canceled status indicates a transaction that was authorized successfully, but not captured.
    • ➞ See Corporate Card: My transaction was canceled
  • Declined: A declined status indicates a transaction that received an error in processing and the transaction did not go through.
    • ➞ See Corporate Card: My transaction was declined
  • Disputed: This transaction was successful, but has been disputed.
  • Pending: A pending status indicates a transaction that has been authorized, but the funds have not been captured yet. If the funds are not captured by the merchant within seven days time, the authorization will automatically be canceled and the funds will be released.
  • Required: A required status indicates a successful transaction that requires a receipt upload. This will show if a transaction is above the threshold dollar amount that your company has set as requiring receipts (by default, it’s set to 75 USD but this may be different depending on your company’s settings).
    • ➞ You will need to submit a receipt for this transaction.

Corporate Card: User roles and permissions

As you invite additional cardholders to your Stripe Corporate Card account, you may want to change the user roles that control what access permissions they have. Stripe Corporate Card roles are set on the team settings page.

There are three roles that provide different levels of Corporate Card access:

Administrator:

  • An administrator will have full access to the Corporate Card Dashboard, statements, and data.
  • An administrator has the same level of access as the Stripe account owner and can view API keys, change account settings, and invite new Corporate Card users. Administrators cannot delete or make changes to the Stripe account owner, but they can connect the Stripe account to Connect platforms.

Analyst

  • An analyst receives view-only access to the Corporate Card Dashboard data and the ability to download related reports.
  • An analyst cannot access any account settings or view API keys. They also cannot make changes to Stripe Radar settings.

Cardholder

  • This is the default role for new users invited to Stripe Corporate Card, and is a Corporate Card specific user role.
  • A cardholder will only have access to their personal credit card information, and cannot view company-wide Corporate Card data or reports.

How to set, delete, or modify a cardholder spending limit

If you are an administrator on the Corporate Card account, you can set, adjust, or remove card-specific limits for a cardholder by following the steps below:

  • Go to the Cardholders section of your Corporate Card Dashboard.
  • Select the cardholder name to pull up the details specific to their card.
  • Under the “Authorization Controls” section, select the Edit button.
  • Under “Spending Limits”, you will see the current spending limit set on this card (by amount, interval, and categories).
  • To set a spending limit, click Add.
  • To remove a spending limit, click on the icon.
  • To adjust a spending limit, first remove the current spending limit by clicking on the icon, and then click Add to set a new one.

If there is no specified spending limit on the card, the card spending limit will automatically default to the company’s overall credit limit.

Additional Information

  • You also have the option to block specific merchant categories.

Integrate your Corporate Card with Expensify

With the Expensify integration enabled, Stripe will synchronize your Corporate Card transactions to Expensify.

To enable the integration:

  • View your Corporate Card settings in the Dashboard
  • Under Product Integrations, click Enable next to Expensify

Once enabled, you will receive an email from Expensify with further instructions in the next 1-2 days.

Additional Information

  • Transactions are synchronized once they are confirmed.
  • Pending or declined transactions will not be synced to Expensify.
  • Receipts uploaded to Stripe will not be synced to Expensify.

Integrate your Corporate Card with Xero

Xero

Stripe can automatically sync your transactions to Xero.

To enable the integration:

  • View your Corporate Card settings in the Dashboard
  • Under Product Integrations, click Connect next to Xero
  • Login to your Xero account
  • Grant Stripe the ability to share your Corporate Card transaction data for all cardholders with Xero
  • Upon being redirected back to the Stripe dashboard, you will be prompted to select an existing Xero bank account to use for syncing your Corporate Card transactions, or you can select the option to have a new Xero bank account created.

Once you select “Connect,” Stripe will sync your Corporate Card transaction data for all cardholders linked to your Corporate Card account so you can view your Corporate Card transaction data in your Xero account. Selecting “disable” stops future data-sharing. Please review Xero’s Privacy Policy.

Transactions

Transactions are synchronized at the end of the day they are confirmed. This means pending transactions will not appear on your Xero account, and all transactions that do appear in Xero are final and will no longer change.

Statements

Statements are created for each day. Once a day, a new statement will be created in Xero containing the transactions that were confirmed that day. If there is a day where no new transactions are confirmed, there won’t be a statement created for that day. Since statements contain only confirmed transactions, statements are final and will not change.

Order your Card

You can also order a physical card for in-person transactions in the Corporate Card Dashboard.

Activate your Card

Although your virtual card is available to use immediately, you must activate your physical card before it can be used.

You can activate your physical card once in the following ways:

  • Responding to the text reminder with the word “Activate”
  • Clicking on Activate from your Dashboard.

Additional Information

Reporting an unauthorized charge on your Stripe Corporate Card

If you notice a charge on your Corporate Card that you did not authorize, you can dispute the transaction through the Corporate Card dashboard:

  • Log on to your Dashboard and select the Transactions page under Corporate Card.
  • Select the “…” option from the top right (located under Export).
  • Select Dispute Transaction and provide the required information to submit.

In the case of unauthorized charges on your card, you should also report the card as compromised immediately in order to prevent further fraudulent charges. See Replacements for lost or stolen cards.

The cardholder or any administrator on the Corporate Card account can report the card as stolen or lost.

Dashboard

Compare Dashboard exports to financial reports

Learn about data sources and why some reports show different numbers.

Dashboard exports reflect real-time data. Reports undergo data processing, which delays availability.

The specific timing of report availability depends on the report. When comparing these data sources, check that data from the same time period has been fully processed in both systems.

Differences between the data may stem from several other factors, such as:

  • Different time periods being compared
  • Different time zones used in calculations
  • Variation in which data are included/excluded in each data
  • Other factors specific to each export/report type

Comparing exports from the Transactions page to Reports

Use reports, such as the Balance Summary Report for accounting and financial reconciliation of your Stripe account.

The Transactions page is recommended for finding a specific payment and performing actions on them.

Differences between these two data sources are expected.

These variations stems from several factors including the time periods compared, the time zones used in calculations, which fees are included in the reports, and other reporting parameters.

Comparing payouts from Balances and the Balance Summary report

You can use two different methods to review your list of payouts:

  • Balances Export: The Balances page Payouts tab
  • Balance Summary Report: The Balance Summary report Payouts section

For accurate comparison between these reports, follow these guidelines:

  • Set both exports to use the UTC time zone for consistency
  • Select identical date ranges for both dashboard pages
  • Compare the payout amounts, dates, and frequency to verify alignment

The Payout Reconciliation report is available for financial reconciliation when automatic payouts are enabled. This report helps you reconcile the transactions included in each payout.

Comparing the All Activity export to the Balance Summary Report

These two reports show your account’s financial activity, but with a key difference:

  • Balance Summary Report: The Balance Change From Activity section of the report excludes payouts from its data.
  • All Activity Export: Includes payouts in its data.
Balance Summary Report

To download the Balance Change From Activity section, navigate to the Balance Summary report, find the Balance change from activity section and click Export.

All Activity export
  • From the Balances page, click the All Activity tab, click on Export, select UTC for the time zone, then click Export to download the All Activity Report
  • Once downloaded, open the file, then filter on Type to exclude any payout transactions
  • The filtered All Activity report should now match the Balance Summary Report

Why your Dashboard balance doesn’t match your financial reports

Your Dashboard balance and your financial reports (Balance Summary Report, Payout Reconciliation Report, Activity Report) are structured differently, so you can’t directly compare them.

The Dashboard balance is a real-time snapshot of your current funds, broken into up to three categories:

  • Available: Funds ready to pay out
  • Pending: Funds still within the settlement window
  • Reserved: Funds held by Stripe for risk purposes

Financial reports show aggregate balance movements (charges, payouts, refunds, fees, disputes) over a defined time period. No line item or column in any financial report directly corresponds to the available, pending, or reserved balance on your Dashboard.

Customize the time zone on the Dashboard

You can set your dashboard time zone from your account settings.

Additional Information

  • This will only affect the times displayed in your dashboard and will not affect your reporting exports, the times returned by the API, or the timing of your subscriptions and transfers. These will remain in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time).

Default time zone setting

The default time zone in your Stripe account is based on the location in which your Stripe account was registered. For example, if your account was set up with a San Francisco-based business address, your dashboard will reflect times according Pacific Time.

Additional Information

  • If you are creating a new Stripe account while logged into an existing account, the new account will inherit the time zone of the existing account.
  • To change your time zone, see Customize the Time Zone on the Dashboard.

Enabling notifications on the Stripe Dashboard mobile app

  • Navigate to Global settings > Notification settings from the list of menu options.
  • Tap the toggle to turn notifications on or off for each of your merchant accounts.

Additional troubleshooting

Push notifications will only work if you also allow notifications for Stripe in the general Settings of your Phone (Settings > Notifications). Read more about modifying your notification permissions for your operating system: iOS, Android.

If you still aren’t receiving push notifications, you can also try the following:

Export customer data without the payment details

The Stripe data migration team can only assist with customer data exports when the request is for the customer along with the associated payment method details (cards, ACH, etc.).

From the Stripe Dashboard, you can export customer details without the payment method details by following these steps:

  • Use the upper-right Filter button as needed, based on whatever parameters you’d like to build the list on
  • Click the export button in the upper right corner

Google login isn’t supported on Dashboard mobile app or the Stripe Terminal app

Google login credentials aren’t supported on the Dashboard mobile app or the Stripe Terminal app. To log in, set a password for your Stripe account:

Use your new password to log in to the Dashboard mobile app.

Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) preparation and resources

As of 14 September 2019, new authentication requirements are being introduced for online payments in Europe as part of the second Payments Services Directive (PSD2). Payments where both the business and the customer’s bank are located in the European Economic Area (EEA) need to meet the new Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) requirements. This means adding an extra layer of security for customers making purchases online. Businesses with European Stripe accounts charging European customers may need to update their Stripe integration to support the additional authentication requirements.

Below you can find some of the most common questions on SCA. Read our technical docs to start integrating our SCA-ready solutions.

Taxes on Stripe fees for Mexico based businesses

For Stripe account holders in Mexico, value-added tax (Impuesto al Valor Agregado in Spanish, referred to as IVA) applies to all Stripe fees at the prevailing standard rate. The IVA charge is applied in addition to Stripes product and service fees.

Since April 1st, 2023, Stripe has been issuing monthly IVA invoices (version 4.0) to account holders that comply with the requirements needed to create electronic invoices (CFDI). If your tax information has been updated in the SAT official records in any of the following cases, please update your tax information at Stripe Dashboard :

  • If your Legal Name and RFC have been updated, you will need to update your details in your Tax details to match exactly with the details in your Constancia de Situación Fiscal.
  • If your business address or ownership details have been updated, you will need to update your details in your Business Information.
  • Once your details have been updated, you will need to upload your Constancia de Situación Fiscal again in your Stripe Dashboard.

If you fail to upload your Constancia de Situación Fiscal and update your tax information through your Stripe Dashboard, Stripe will be unable to issue your monthly IVA Invoice. Instead, Stripe will include your fees in a monthly global invoice issued to the general public. Where this is the case it may not be possible for you to obtain certain tax deductions or credits for your company.

In order to comply with the safety and privacy of your data, Stripe will only accept documents sent through your Stripe Dashboard.

Check the articles below to learn more about your monthly tax invoices.

  • Understanding your tax invoice: Understanding your monthly tax invoice
  • Downloading your Tax invoice: Accessing Tax invoices on Stripe fees for accounts based in Mexico
  • Reconciling your tax invoices against stripe fees reporting: How to reconcile your tax invoice in Mexico
  • FAQs about CFDI 4.0: Accounts from Mexico: Update your tax information

Time zone customization: changes to reports

Note: this functionality is not yet available to all users.

Financial reports on the Balance and Reconciliation tab now generate reports in your Stripe account’s time zone by default.

How to return to using UTC

If you generated reports prior to the addition of time zone selection, the only time zone available was UTC. You can return to using UTC on financial reports for this session by selecting UTC from date range time zone selector shown below. You will need to reselect UTC if you navigate away from the financial reports page and later return.

You can also set your account time zone setting to UTC. This will affect all date and times in the Dashboard except for products that specifically note otherwise.

Columns that were previously date time values in UTC now have a duplicate column with the time offset to the requested time zone. You can distinguish by the _utc in the column header.

The default column sets for reports now include the time zone adjusted column instead of the UTC column. You can select the UTC columns by selecting Custom from the dropdown and checking the boxes for the desired columns.

Recommendation to avoid missing transactions

If you have downloaded reports in UTC in previous periods, we recommend that you download the current period in both UTC and in your time zone and use both reports for reconciling the current period. It might seem like there are duplicate or missing transactions if the previous period report and the current period report are in different time zones.

Example: if you download a report ending at end of day December 31, 2019 in UTC and a report with period start of start of day January 1, 2020 in Europe/Helsinki, some of your Stripe transactions would not appear on either report due to the time windows.

Changes to subscriptions

Subscribing to a daily, weekly, or monthly e-mail will now notify you when the data for the interval requested is available based on your Stripe account’s time zone instead of UTC.

Don’t see the the DDI Instructions?

Uploading photo of government-issued ID FAQ

Stripe may require users to upload a photo of a government-issued photo ID and a selfie for identity verification to the Dashboard. The photos must be clear and well-lit without any obstructions. Use a mobile device’s camera for better quality.

In some cases, Stripe will require you to upload an image of your photo ID and selfie to confirm your identity. You’ll need to take a photo of an accepted form of ID, such as a driver’s license or passport. Sometimes we’ll also need to capture an image of your face in addition. Due to the highly sensitive nature of your verification documents, Stripe can only accept documents which are uploaded through the Dashboard. Do not send documents by email.

You’ll need:

  • A valid government-issued photo ID document.
    • ID cannot be expired.
    • ID must not be redacted, altered, or damaged. All edges of ID must be visible.
    • Check that your ID type is supported. Select the appropriate country in the drop-down.
    • The information in these documents must match the information on your Stripe account. Confirm that the Stripe account personal information in your Dashboard is correct before documents are uploaded. Clicking Edit beside your personal details to make any changes.
    • Image must be in color
    • Image must be in .png or .jpg format
  • Mobile device with a camera. Cameras on mobile devices typically take higher-quality photos than a webcam.

A better quality image dramatically increases your chance of being successfully verified.

  • Capture a clear image. Ensure images are not too dark or bright and don’t have a glare. Hold steady and allow your camera to focus to avoid blurry photos.
  • Do not block any part of your ID document in the image. Lay it on a flat surface to take the photo.
  • Do not block any part of your face. Remove sunglasses, masks, or other accessories.
  • Find a location with ambient lighting. Avoid spaces with strong overhead lights that cast a shadow on your face or ID document. Avoid sitting directly in front of a bright light which can wash out your face and add a glare to your ID document.

ID verification link isn’t working?

If the link to complete ID verification isn’t working, try the following:

  • Restart your browser
  • Clear your browser cache
  • Use a different browser

Didn’t receive the text message?

If you don’t receive a text message, you can use a QR code instead to access the link. In the Dashboard there is an option to display a QR code on the screen. Then use your phone’s camera (if QR code detection is supported) or other barcode scanning app to scan the code and access the link.

Problems accessing your computer’s webcam?

Check that you’ve given Stripe permission to access your webcam—if you block permissions to your camera, refer to Chrome, Safari, or Edge documentation on allowing access to use your webcam.

If you don’t have a webcam, in the Dashboard there is an option to switch to another device. You’ll be prompted to enter your mobile phone number and Stripe will send a link to your phone to start the process.

Problems with the photograph?

  • Be sure that you’re well lit from the front, not the back.
  • Make sure that your fingers are not covering any parts of the ID.
  • If you are using your mobile phone, try laying the ID on a flat surface in a well lit room.

Problems uploading an image file

To upload an image file, if not prompted directly, select Other Options and select upload images.

View your support cases from the Dashboard

From the Support center you can view active and closed support cases, upload files requested by Stripe, and respond to ongoing cases. The Support center is found under the Help menu (question mark icon) in the top right hand corner of the Dashboard.

To respond to an existing support case

  • In the Support center, find the case in the Active tab of the Support messages table
  • Click on the case to view the case details.
  • At the bottom of the case details page is a text box where you can type your reply.

Data Pipeline

Connecting Stripe to your data warehouse or cloud storage

Stripe Data Pipeline is a no-code product that can send all your Stripe data to your data storage destination on an automated and ongoing basis.

  • What data storage destinations can I connect to using Data Pipeline?
  • What data is available via Data Pipeline?
  • How quickly is data made available in my data storage destination?
  • How is historical data managed and loaded?
  • Are there any data retention policies?
  • Is there any sort of change data capture? How can I consume incremental data between full loads?
  • Does Stripe perform data delivery and completeness checks?
  • Will I be notified of issues with my data delivery or planned maintenance?
  • Are there any limits to the amount of data that Data Pipeline can load?

What data storage destinations can I connect to using Data Pipeline?

Data Pipeline supports direct integration to Snowflake and Amazon Redshift data warehouses.

It also supports connection to Google Cloud Storage, Amazon S3, and Azure Blob Storage. From there, you can send your data to various destinations, including additional data warehouses, such as Google BigQuery, Databricks, and more.

What data is available via Data Pipeline?

All Core API, Connect Core API, and Analytical datasets are available via Data Pipeline.

TheStripe Data Schema as well as our docs have a detailed view of all the data that is made available to you and how it’s organized.

How quickly is data made available in my data storage destination?

Details on data freshness are available in our docs.

How is historical data managed and loaded?

Every time fresh data is delivered to your warehouse, it will include your full dataset—from when you started on Stripe to the freshest data batch available. You are not charged for historical data.

Are there any data retention policies?

It is up to you to decide on a data retention policy and implement it. We recommend keeping data for at least seven days, but many merchants choose to only retain the last few shares to save on cloud storage costs.

Is there any sort of change data capture? How can I consume incremental data between full loads?

We do not currently support incremental data loads for our cloud storage destinations. Every table has a batch_timestamp field, which is populated with the time stamp for when data is processed through Data Pipeline.

Does Stripe perform data delivery and completeness checks?

Stripe conducts row-level checks to ensure data integrity. If any checks fail, the data won’t be delivered until complete.

Will I be notified of issues with my data delivery or planned maintenance?

When signing up for Data Pipeline, you have the option to share a contact email to receive critical updates on the status of your data processing. We suggest using a team alias so that multiple members of your team are notified about issues.

Additionally, a webhook is available to notify your system when data delivery is successful. Details on how to set up webhooks are available in our docs.

Are there any limits to the amount of data that Data Pipeline can load?

No. Data Pipeline is designed to manage large data loads. We currently accommodate some of Stripe’s largest users’ volume of 4TB of data per load. There are no rate limits.
