Submit a Terminal card reader warranty claim

Stripe offers a one-year limited warranty on all card reader hardware purchased through Stripe Terminal.

If your card reader is broken, malfunctioning, or has a hardware issue:

  • Users in Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Norway, Singapore, or Switzerland: Contact us from the Stripe account that placed the original hardware order. Include the serial number of your device and a description of the issue in your warranty replacement claim.
  • Users in other countries where Terminal is supported: Submit a warranty claim in the Dashboard.

If your platform placed the hardware order, you can submit warranty claims from your platform Dashboard.

If the hardware order was placed by a connected account, platforms can submit a warranty claim on their behalf by using the Dashboard Login as feature to access their account and submitting the claim from there.

Team members with Administrator and Terminal Specialist roles can submit warranty claims from the Stripe account that was used to place the hardware order.

Supporting dual-network debit cards in Australia

What is a dual-network debit card?

Most Australian-issued debit payment cards display two debit payment networks – eftpos (eftpos Payments Australia Limited) and another card network (for example, Mastercard debit, Visa debit). Payments using a card displaying two debit payment networks may be processed through either network, regardless of the logo displayed when a customer enters their payment information.

What is least-cost routing / merchant-choice routing?

As part of its Conclusions to the Review of Retail Payments Regulation in October 2021, the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) expects all acquirers, payment facilitators, and gateways to offer and promote least-cost routing functionality (LCR, also called merchant-choice routing) to Australian merchants in both device-present (in-person) and device-not-present (online) environments.

LCR occurs when a customer makes a payment with their dual-network debit card and the transaction is deliberately routed to particular debit networks rather than letting all transactions flow to the default network as set by card issuers or card schemes. The choice of debit network may be based on several different factors, such as which network is the lowest cost to accept, or whether the merchant has a particular network preference.

How does Stripe implement least-cost routing / merchant-choice routing?

Stripe automatically implements least-cost routing for all of its Australian merchants.

Transactions made using eftpos dual-network debit cards will generally route through eftpos (based on lowest average costs), provided that the transaction type can be supported by eftpos.

For online environments, we recommend that you inform your customers that whenever they use a dual-network debit card, payments may be processed through either debit network. For guidelines on best practice, refer to our eftpos online documentation.

If you’d like to opt-out of least-cost routing, and require that eftpos is never the default network for any payments, contact support.

While Stripe endeavors to route such transactions through eftpos, other factors may impact which network a transaction is routed through, including: (1) technical availability, and (2) authorization rate considerations. Changes in the network that route these transactions may result in changes to merchant transaction costs. For further information, refer to the “integration” sections of our in-person and online eftpos documentation.

Is least-cost routing / merchant-choice routing compatible with Tap to Pay?

Least-cost routing is supported in Australia on Tap to Pay on Android on Android SDK 4.3+ and Tap to Pay on iPhone on iOS SDK 4.7+.

How does the Link Payment Method affect least-cost routing?

Adding the Link Payment Method to your checkout page auto-fills your customers’ payment and shipping information to enable faster checkouts. If your customer has saved a dual-network debit card to their Link account, the payment may be processed through either network in the same way as if your customer chooses to input their card details at checkout.

Tap to Pay on iPhone or Android and Stripe Terminal

Tap to Pay lets users accept in-person contactless payments with a compatible consumer device and the Stripe Terminal SDK. It requires familiarity with the Terminal SDK and either Android or iOS expertise. See our iOS technical integration documentation and Android technical integration documentation.

Where is Tap to Pay available?

Find out which countries Tap to Pay is available in on Regional considerations or in the technical integration documentation linked above.

If you would like to use Tap to Pay in your country and it’s not currently supported, let us know. We’ll let you know once we’re able to offer this where you are.

What are the device requirements for integrating Tap to Pay?

See supported devices for the device requirements for Tap to Pay on iPhone. iPads do not have NFC reading capabilities are not supported at this time.

See supported devices for the device requirements for Tap to Pay on Android and a list of supported Android devices with custom UIs.

What payment methods are supported with Tap to Pay?

See supported card brands for information on which payment methods are available per reader.

What is the pricing?

Visit our Pricing page for current pricing.

Are Tap to Pay transactions routed as card-present transactions?

Yes. Tap to Pay transactions can be identified in the Dashboard as “Card Present” payments like all other Terminal transactions. As with Stripe Terminal, merchants who use Tap to Pay to accept payment cards are not liable for any fraudulent-type disputes filed for such transactions.

Stripe Terminal Tap to Pay and PCI compliance

Stripe Terminal, including Tap to Pay, by default provides E2EE. Users leveraging Tap to Pay have access to a pre-filled SAQ C document, directly in your Dashboard under Compliance Settings.

Note: Tap to Pay is not supported for use with P2PE.

Is there a way to identify Tap to Pay transactions through the Dashboard? Does Tap to Pay offer the same functionality as other devices from Stripe Terminal?

Tap to Pay devices have the same functionality as other Terminal devices in the Dashboard. For example, Tap to Pay transactions can be identified in the Dashboard as “Card Present” payments like all other Terminal transactions. Additionally, you can see Tap to Pay Readers in the Terminal Readers section of the Dashboard.

Is there a way to reconcile the active device count on a Stripe account against Tap to Pay billing?

At this time, we do not offer this functionality.

Is PIN supported through Tap to Pay for transactions that exceed contactless limits?

Tap to Pay on iPhone supports accepting PIN in the 2.23 and above versions of the Terminal iOS SDK.

Tap to Pay on Android supports accepting PIN in the 4.3.0 and above versions of the Terminal Android SDK.

Regional contactless limits are noted at our Support Q&A page. Note: Generally there are no transaction limits for digital wallets like Apple Pay and Google Pay.

Can you collect payment using a physical Terminal card reader as a backup option?

Not all customers will have a contactless payment method. In this event or in the event of a decline, users can continue to collect a payment by switching from Tap to Pay to a Terminal card reader. However, users can only have one active connection to a reader at a time. So you’ll need to disconnect the card reader if it’s already connected.

Does Tap to Pay work on tablets?

Tap to Pay requires NFC technology which many tablets do not have.

Tap to Pay on iPhone does not work on iPads as they currently do not support NFC.

Tap to Pay on Android works on Android tablets that meet our device requirements.

Is there a way to identify the cardholder name for Tap to Pay transactions?

The cardholder name is typically not available on contactless payments. Visit the API reference to understand which transaction-specific details are available for Terminal transactions, including Tap to Pay.

Integration Questions

Does a user need to integrate with the Terminal SDK?

Yes, users must first have completed the Terminal SDK integration prior to integrating Tap to Pay. See the iOS or Android documentation for specifics.

When building your Terminal integration, do you need to install the Terminal SDK first before the Tap to Pay SDK(s)?

Yes. To access Tap to Pay ’s functionality users need to install two sets of SDKs. Users must first have a complete Terminal SDK integration prior to integrating with the Tap to Pay SDK(s). Check out our iOS or Android documentation for specifics.

Does Terminal offer a pre-built mobile POS application that users can leverage?

You can accept in-person Tap to Pay payments using the Stripe Terminal app.

If a user takes a Tap to Pay device to another country that isn’t supported (ie: from the US to BR), would the functionality be automatically blocked? Do additional restrictions need to be set up on their application based around location?

We collect GPS data for location verification during Terminal transactions. Tap to Pay will not work if brought across borders. Our system will automatically deny the transaction if a new country is detected. No additional integration work is needed for this feature.

Can a user simulate Tap to Pay transactions in the Terminal simulator?

Yes, users can currently simulate the payment collection flow within the iOS and Android simulators.

Is Tap to Pay compatible with apps built in React Native?

Yes, Tap to Pay is supported on applications built on React Native.

Is the ability to save card details for online reuse compatible with Tap to Pay transactions?

Yes. Tap to Pay supports existing Terminal functionality to save card details for future online reuse. The Save Card functionality applies only to physical cards, not mobile wallets.

Is tipping compatible with Tap to Pay?

On-reader tipping is not compatible with Tap to Pay. Users are free to implement their own tipping screen before collecting payment or users can use the post-auth flow for tipping after payment collection. Post-auth tipping must be completed within 3 minutes after payment collection. Due to this function, we recommend presenting tipping before collecting payment for a smoother user experience.

Is Offline mode compatible with Tap to Pay?

No. Offline mode is not compatible with Tap to Pay.

Is there any way to restrict card types at the Tap to Pay?

No. We don’t offer the functionality to restrict cards at the Tap to Pay level.

Do Stripe test cards work with Tap to Pay?

Yes, learn more at test Stripe Terminal.

How do I test PIN with Tap to Pay on iPhone for transactions that exceed contactless limits?

Use physical test cards with transaction amounts ending in .03 to test PIN entry. This testing method works with Tap to Pay on iPhone using Stripe accounts based in regions where PIN is accepted such as Canada and Germany. It won’t work in the US and other regions where PIN isn’t accepted. An online_or_offline_pin_required error is returned after the card is tapped if you attempt a transaction ending in .03 using a US-based Stripe account with Tap to Pay on iPhone.

What does it mean if I am seeing an on_behalf_of error?

If you are using the on_behalf_of parameter in your PaymentIntent, provide the Connected Account ID in the SCPLocalMobileConnectionConfiguration. See our iOS or Android docs for full details.

Can I customize the UI for the tap screen?

You can’t customize the UI for Tap to Pay on iPhone.

Tap to Pay on Android has some customization options that allow you to override the colors of the tap zone, error message, and success animation, and the position of the tap zone indicator. These customization options let you align the tap screen with your own brand identity and theme. See our Android docs for full details.

Does the user have to customize the tap zones in their integration for each device type?

For Tap to Pay on Android, Stripe handles the transaction UI. The tap zone prompt is customized to where the NFC chip is on each device (for example, top right, top left, or middle). If the tap zone isn’t known, the default screen is used. There is no integration work required to customize the tap zones, though you can manually set this position using the setTaptoPayUxConfiguration API.

What is the expected level of effort required to integrate with this library?

Once the user has completed the standard integration with Terminal’s iOS or Android SDK(s), the respective integrations for Tap to Pay on iOS or Android is fairly simple and straightforward. On average it takes one engineer less than two weeks to complete.

Tap to Pay on iPhone Related Questions

For Frequently Asked Questions related to Tap to Pay on iPhone, see Apple’s Merchant FAQ.

How is initial onboarding handled for iPhone devices?

Users will be presented with Apple’s Tap to Pay on iPhone Terms and Conditions the first time they connect to the local reader. In order to register with Apple, merchants must specify a valid Apple ID representing their business before accepting the terms presented by Apple. Note that this flow only needs to be performed once per Stripe account. This flow will be skipped for all subsequent connections using the same Stripe account across all devices.

To learn more about merchant linking, go to the Tap to Pay on iPhone Business Information section in Apple’s Tap to Pay on iPhone FAQ.

Before using a device to read payment cards, you need to configure it appropriately. This configuration must be done on every device using Tap to Pay on iPhone for the first time. The initial configuration of a device can take up to two minutes. Any subsequent configuration updates typically take just a few seconds. See the ‘Handle device setup’ section for more details.

Can I accept the Tap to Pay on iPhone’s Terms and Conditions (ToS) before connecting to the reader?

Yes, you can onboard merchants and accept Apple’s ToS online by using the Terminal Onboarding Links API. Both individual merchants and platforms for their connected accounts can use the API to accept the ToS on the web, which prevents the in-the app ToS prompt when connecting to the reader for the first time.

Why is my Terminal Onboarding Links redirect_url returning “The token from your payment service provider isn’t valid”?

If you’ve already generated a redirect URL and started the process to link an Apple account, you must pass in the allow_relinking=true field in order to restart the linking process, even if you haven’t finished accepting the ToS.

Are the Tap to Pay on iPhone’s Terms and Conditions (ToS) acceptance steps transparently handled by the Terminal SDK?

If the ToS aren’t already accepted online, the Terms of Service for Tap to Pay on iPhone will show up automatically on the first local reader connection for a given account. This is implicitly handled by the Terminal SDK and no additional code is required to trigger the Terms of Service flow.

When do the Tap to Pay on iPhone’s Terms and Conditions (ToS) steps happen?

The Terms of Service for Tap to Pay on iPhone is presented on the first connectLocalMobileReader for a given connect subaccount. Once the Terms of Service are accepted, it will no longer show up for the given account. Alternatively, use the Terminal Onboarding Links API to accept Apple’s ToS on the web instead of within an application.

Apple’s docs mention a requirement that “Only an admin user can accept The Terms and Conditions on behalf of a merchant.” Does the merchant need to do anything to indicate that a user is authorized to accept the T&Cs?

We recommend that merchants provide guidance during user onboarding to ensure that the authorized merchant is accepting the terms.

The best practices recommend connecting to the reader in the background on app startup. How do I prevent the Tap to Pay on iPhone’s Terms and Conditions (ToS) from showing up when users launch the app for the first time?

Merchants can set the tosAcceptancePermitted parameter to NO in the connectionConfig when calling connectLocalMobileReader in the background. If a user has not yet accepted the ToS, this connection will fail with an exception. We recommend that merchants handle this exception and guide the user to a separate explicit onboarding flow where connectLocalMobileReader is called with the parameter enabled and where the authorized merchant can accept the ToS.

When the Apple TTP screen pops up and shows the business name, how configurable is that for Platforms? Is it specific to the exact DBA of the connected account?

Platforms can configure the business name. We use the connect account name as the default but you can override this should you choose to do so. You should ensure to specify the correct business name.

Does Stripe support implementations where a merchant directly uses Apple’s proximityReader API?

We currently don’t support directly using Apple’s proximityReader API. Using the proximityReader properly relies on a direct relationship with Apple in order to issue reader connection tokens.

Are there options available for customizing the Tap to Pay on iPhone User Interface?

No. The Tap to Pay on iPhone UI that is triggered when your point-of-sale application is ready to collect a payment. It cannot be customized.

Do you need to set a location for your mobile device when using Tap to Pay on iPhone? Is this required by Apple?

All Terminal hardware readers are required to set a Location. This is an existing requirement that also applies to Tap to Pay on iPhone.

How do I get my iOS app approved by Apple?

Your Tap to Pay on iPhone application will go through the standard Apple App Store review process. Be sure to consider Apple’s Tap to Pay Human Interface Guidelines when building your app.

How do I request and configure the required entitlement to support Tap to Pay on iPhone?

You can directly request an entitlement from the Apple Developer site.

Tap to Pay on Android related questions

How do I know if my phone supports NFC?

You can confirm your Android device supports NFC by checking your phone’s Settings. If you see an NFC option, it is supported, and just make sure it’s switched on to use Tap to Pay.

When will Discover be supported?

We do not have a timeline for Discover support at this time.

How can I keep up with any relevant SDK changes?

Subscribe to terminal-announce@lists.stripe.com. We are aiming to give at least 3 months heads up for any future changes, but more urgent SDK updates may be required if a critical security vulnerability is discovered in the SDK.

Additionally, Tap to Pay on Android has public changelogs.

Support

I have questions about my Apple ID account, Apple Business Register (ABR) account, and/or iPhone hardware.

Users can find support for Apple related issues at the following resources:

  • Tap to Pay on iPhone Developer site
  • Tap to Pay on iPhone Merchant site

Terminal

With Stripe Terminal, you can integrate Stripe payments into your existing in-person checkout flow or build in-person payments into your native mobile or web-based application. Terminal comes with easy-to-use SDKs and APIs for modern development environments, pre-certified readers, Tap to Pay on iPhone and Android, and tools for ordering and managing readers from the Stripe Dashboard. It works seamlessly with other Stripe products, letting you build a SaaS platform or marketplace using Connect or initiate subscriptions in-store with Billing. Terminal reduces the burden of compliance, deployment, and logistics—so you can focus on building your ideal in-person payments experience.

Terminal card reader returns

If you purchased your reader directly from Stripe

Users in the US, Canada, Australia & EMEA (excluding Norway & Switzerland)

  • Navigate to the Hardware orders section in your Dashboard here.
  • Select the order you want to return and select the Return Order button.
  • Provide the reason for the return and the serial number of the device you are returning.
  • Follow the prompts to generate a return label.
  • Pack the reader in its original packaging (with all accessories) and attach the return label.
  • Ship the package back to Stripe using the provided return label.

All other geographies

  • Navigate to the Hardware orders section in your Dashboard here.
  • Select the order you want to return.
  • Click Contact Support to automatically send us your order details.
  • Be sure to provide the serial number of the device you are returning and the reason for return in your message.

Please note: We can only accept refunds for orders in original packaging (along with all accessories) within 30 days of the date of purchase. See here for warranty details.

If you purchased your reader via a Connect platform and not directly from Stripe

Please contact the platform directly to request a return or refund of the Terminal reader. Stripe is unable to facilitate the return or a refund of a Terminal reader bought via a platform.

Terminal hardware deliveries to outlying territories of supported countries

Stripe availability varies for businesses located in an outlying territory of a supported countries. See Stripe availability for outlying territories of supported countries.

What should I expect when receiving a Stripe Terminal reader in an outlying territory?

The delivery and import process can vary by territory and shipment.

Stripe does not charge customs duties, import taxes, VAT, or customs-clearance fees at checkout for overseas territories that Stripe identifies as Designated Markets before you place your order.

These charges are not included in your checkout total and may be assessed after your order has been submitted and collected separately by the local government authority, carrier, customs broker, or other service provider.

Your carrier may contact you by phone to arrange delivery or discuss import charges. You may need to pay these charges before your reader can be handed over, and you may not receive advance notice before the delivery driver arrives.

Will I need to pay customs fees or import taxes?

You may be asked to pay local import taxes, customs fees, or carrier handling charges before your reader can be handed over. The amount and type of charges can vary by territory and shipment, and some deliveries may have no additional charges.

Potential charges and invoice line items include the following. (Note - Descriptions in French are included to users identify them on an invoice):

  • Customs release charge (Crédit d’enlèvement): a charge associated with the customs release credit arrangement
  • UPS administrative or processing fee (Frais de dossier UPS (GP&MQ))
  • Local import tax (dock dues) (Octroi de mer or Octroi de mer externe)
  • Regional import tax (regional dock dues) (Octroi de mer régional or Octroi de mer externe régional)
  • VAT on goods (TVA marchandise)
  • Customs clearance agent fees (Honoraires agréés en douanes)
  • Customs duty (Droit de douane communautaire). This line item may appear with a zero amount.

These invoice descriptions are examples. This is not an exhaustive list of charges that may apply to every shipment. Users must check their invoice for charges and amounts applicable to their delivery.

How do I pay a delivery or import charges?

The carrier will tell you how to pay any charges. Payment may be requested at time of delivery. Check the accepted payment methods with UPS or Fedex and keep a copy of the invoice and payment receipt.

Will I need to complete import documents or show identification?

Requirements may vary. You may be asked to show government-issued identification, even if no import forms are required. Follow your carrier’s instructions and confirm whether you need to provide any documents or identification.

What should I check on the invoice?

Check that the invoice is for your shipment and that the recipient details, items, and charges are correct. If you receive an incorrect invoice or something does not match your shipment, ask the carrier or customs contact that issued it to clarify or correct it before you pay. Keep the corrected invoice and any payment receipt for your records.

Terminal in Japan

Stripe Terminal is available in public preview to users in Japan. In Japan, Terminal supports in-person payments in Japanese yen (JPY). See our Terminal docs on how to integrate.

Supported devices

Payment methods

Additionally, the Stripe Reader S700/S710 supports QR code payments.

To request access to the PayPay private preview, reach out to our sales team.

Delivery for Terminal hardware orders can take longer than 3 business days. You can track your order to see when it will arrive.

If you have a problem with your device, you can replace it as part of your one-year limited warranty.

Contact us from the Stripe account that placed the original hardware order to report your issue. You’ll need to provide the serial number of the device along with a description of the issue you are experiencing.

Terminal in Mexico

Stripe Terminal is available in public preview to users in Mexico. In Mexico, Terminal supports in-person payments in Mexican pesos (MXN). To integrate Terminal, see our docs.

Devices

Payment methods

Users can accept voucher cards (vales de despansa) co-branded through Visa or Mastercard as a payment method through Terminal. Acceptance for voucher cards is based on the MCC (merchant category code) assigned to a user’s Stripe account.

Terminal doesn’t support OXXO Pay or Meses sin intereses (MSI) as an in-person payment method in Mexico.

Reader Registration

Card readers must be registered to a Terminal location (tml_) as part of set up. Terminal locations require a valid address and must be formatted correctly for regulatory reporting purposes in Mexico.

Hardware ordering and returns

When ordering Terminal hardware users in Mexico need to provide their correct shipping address.

Shipping addresses must include the following:

  • Recipient’s Name
  • Street Name and Building Number
  • Colonia (Neighborhood)
  • 5-digit Postal Code
  • City/Municipality
  • State
  • Mexico as the Country

Users are also required to provide a valid email address along with their phone number and shipping address when submitting their hardware order to ensure successful delivery. Provinces aren’t used, and a recipient’s phone number and tax ID (RFC) or CURP are legally required for regulatory purposes.

Delivery for Terminal hardware orders may take up to 7 business days to complete delivery. Users can track their order through the Dashboard to see when it will arrive.

Warranty

If you have a problem with your device, you can replace it as part of the one-year limited warranty. Contact us from the Stripe account that placed the original hardware order to report your issue. You’ll need to provide the serial number of the device along with a description of the issue you are experiencing.

Terminal server-driven integration

Server-driven integration mode enables you to build in-person payment experiences using the Stripe API, instead of requiring the Android, iOS, or JavaScript SDK.

What are the benefits of server-driven integration?

With server-driven integration, you can:

  • Use Terminal even if your infrastructure doesn’t support our native iOS, Android, or JS SDKs.
  • Build an integration that’s powered by your own middleware or cloud-based infrastructure.
  • Improve reader network connections using an internet connection instead of the local area network.

This integration mode requires using the BBPOS WisePOS E, Stripe Reader S700/S710, Terminal’s screen-enabled smart readers which supports both countertop and mobile use cases, or the Stripe Reader T600 Terminal’s countertop reader.

What are the limitations?

Server-driven integration doesn’t support:

  • Stripe Terminal Bluetooth readers
  • Offline payment collection

Where is server-driven available?

See which readers and integration modes you can use in each country.

What’s required to get started?

See our integration documentation and sample integration code.

Can I continue using the Terminal Android, iOS, and JavaScript SDKs?

Yes, we’ll continue supporting and making updates to the Android, iOS, and JavaScript SDKs.

You can choose to use server-driven integration as your only integration mode. You can also choose to use an SDK integration alongside server-driven; the WisePOS E will respond to requests from both integration types depending on preference - no additional configuration is needed.

What are the benefits to network connectivity?

Server-driven allows you to avoid local network issues and DNS issues by using the Stripe API as the intermediary between your point of sale application and the reader.

Terminal support for mobile wallets and contactless cards

You can collect payments using mobile wallets (Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay) and contactless tap-and-pay cards with Stripe Terminal.

  • If you’re using a smart reader, the reader display automatically shows the possible card presentment methods.
  • If you’re using a mobile reader, such as the M2 reader or WisePad 3, and you’re not using a screen, your point-of-sale (POS) app displays the allowed input methods such as Insert to the cardholder. See Handling reader display events.

In supported countries, you can save tapped cards using the SetupIntents API.

Terminal support for PIN debit transactions

Support for PIN transactions on Terminal varies by region.

United States

Terminal processes co-branded debit transactions in the US through the credit card networks (for example, Visa, Mastercard, and Discover). Cards in the US run across credit rails rather than debit rails, and typically don’t require a PIN for cardholder verification.

If a PIN is required, for example, for cards issued internationally, the Stripe Reader S700/S710, Stripe Reader T600, and WisePOS E readers prompt for a PIN. Stripe Reader M2 doesn’t prompt for a PIN, however this doesn’t impede general acceptance. PIN-less transactions can be processed on card readers without a PIN pad.

Co-branded debit cards (which support both a local debit network and the Visa, Mastercard, or Discover networks) are accepted, and make up the vast majority of debit cards issued in the US. Debit cards that don’t support Visa, Mastercard, or Discover co-branding aren’t accepted.

Canada

Terminal processes Interac Debit transactions as PIN debit. Both credit card and Interac debit payments may require customers to enter their PIN on the card reader to complete the transaction.

Europe and Asia Pacific

Terminal processes co-branded debit transactions through the credit card networks and prompts for a PIN when required. In European markets, there are regulatory requirements around PIN authentication for transactions. Read more about PIN and Strong Customer Authentication requirements.

Hong Kong

All debit card transactions in Hong Kong require a PIN. Terminal prompts the customer to enter their PIN.

Credit card and quasi-credit card transactions require a PIN when the transaction amount exceeds the card’s contactless limit.

Australia

eftpos is the interbank network that handles routing of debit payments in Australia. A majority of consumer debit cards in Australia are branded with an eftpos logo and co-branded with Visa or Mastercard. Terminal processes co-branded debit transactions through both the credit card networks and eftpos, depending on the type of transaction. Terminal also supports mono-branded debit cards. In both cases, the Terminal prompts for a PIN when required.

New Zealand

eftpos is the interbank network that handles routing of debit payments in New Zealand. Consumer debit cards in New Zealand are branded with an eftpos logo and may also be co-branded with Visa or Mastercard. Terminal supports co-branded eftpos over the co-brand rails.

Test your Terminal integration

Stripe Terminal requires a developer to build a custom integration. If you’re ready to test that integration, this article covers how to get started with a simulated reader or physical hardware. For setup instructions, review our integration documentation.

Simulated reader

A simulated reader lets you build and test your Terminal integration without a physical card reader. This is useful if your team is still waiting on hardware, readers can’t be shipped to your location, or you want to start building right away.

Physical hardware

Test your Terminal integration using a Stripe pre-certified card reader and a physical test card.

Card reader

You need a physical reader to start processing live transactions.

If you’d rather skip specialized payment hardware, Stripe also supports Tap to Pay on iPhone and Android devices.

Test card

Terminal test cards are designed for use with physical card readers. Purchase Stripe Terminal test cards from the Terminal tab of your Dashboard.

In a sandbox, test cards work regardless of the expiration date printed on the card. Test cards are declined in live mode.

Using Terminal in attended, semi-attended, and unattended retail environments

Stripe Terminal’s pre-certified card readers and Tap to Pay support attended and semi-attended retail environments. For unattended retail environments, Stripe Terminal offers the Verifone UX700. This article explains the difference between these environment types.

Attended and semi-attended environments

Terminal supports these environments.

Attended retail environments have staff available to help customers, either at each device or elsewhere at the location. This includes semi-attended environments, where customers interact with the card reader independently but staff are available in the store or nearby if needed.

  • Traditional point of purchase or mobile point of purchase with a staff member stationed at, or roaming with a mobile card reader.
  • Self-service kiosk with roaming employees nearby at the location, but not one per kiosk.
    • Examples: Grocery self-checkout, movie theater ticketing kiosk, standalone kiosk at a quick-service restaurant, music festival that has 20 self-service kiosks for food wristbands with one staff member nearby.

Unattended environments

The Verifone UX700 is the only unattended device offered through Terminal. Unattended payments for the Verifone UX700 is generally availabile to users in the United States. Availability varies for other regions. If you’re interested in using the Verifone UX700, contact our Sales team.

Unattended retail environments do not have staff on site to help customers if needed. They can also include permanent outdoor devices designed to operate in varying weather conditions.

  • ATMs (automated teller machines)
  • Vending machines
  • Dispensing machines
  • Toll booths
  • Parking meters

Verifone hardware

Stripe supports Verifone card readers as part of Terminal.

Users in the United States can purchase Verifone card readers directly from the hardware shop in their Dashboard. Users in all other countries should reach out to our Sales Team if interested in Verifone hardware.

Users that have purchased Verifone hardware as part of Terminal will need to work Stripe directly for any support requests. Requests made directly to Verifone’s support team may be redirected.

Hardware Refunds

Stripe can’t accept refunds for orders of Verifone card readers.

Verifone card readers purchased through Terminal are final sale and are not eligible for the 30 day refund policy like other hardware.

Warranty Replacements

Verifone hardware purchased through Terminal is eligible for replacement under the one-year limited warranty. Users can submit a warranty claim for their Verifone card reader directly through their Dashboard. Verifone card readers that have been returned to Stripe as part of a warranty claim are subject to inspection upon receipt.

Users are required to send back their nonfunctioning Verifone card reader within 30 days after a warranty claim has been submitted. A prepaid return label for the nonfunctioning device is included in the box with the replacement device.

Users should keep all of the accessories for their Verifone card reader. Replacements for Verifone devices aren’t shipped with additional accessories. If you have damaged accessories, order new accessories through the dashboard.

Users may be charged for the cost of a new device if their Verifone card reader is not received within the 30 days. Users may also be charged for the cost of a new device if the returned Verifone card reader is determined to be functioning and operable after inspection.

Receipt Functions

The Verifone V660p reader uses thermal paper for receipt printing. Thermal receipt paper uses heat to print and does not require ink. Thermal receipt paper rolls are available for purchase through several online retailers.

Thermal receipt paper should meet the following dimensions for use with the Verifone V660p:

  • 2 ¼ inches wide x 50 inches long.
  • Or 57mm wide x 40mm in diameter.

Different size thermal receipt paper rolls will not be compatible with the Verifone V660p.

Verifone V660p

The Verifone V660p reader comes equipped with 2GB of RAM.

Verifone M425/UX700

Users looking to power these devices off or to perform a power cycle will need to fully unplug these devices from their power source and then plug them back in.

Serial Numbers

Verifone devices have a 9-digit numeric serial number that is listed on a sticker on the back of the device. The serial number can be located above the bar code with the line beginning with “S/N”.

What happens if my Terminal card reader is tampered with?

If your card reader detects a possible security breach, it displays a tampered message. The reader permanently locks itself to maintain transaction security and must be replaced.

What causes tampering?

Terminal card readers have built-in mechanisms to detect tampering. This occurs if the reader is:

  • Physically shaken or dropped
  • Exposed to liquids
  • Subject to attempted unauthorized access

Smart readers

If you see on-screen messages like those shown on the BBPOS WisePOS E or Stripe Reader S700/S710, your device has detected tampering.

Mobile readers

The following indicators signal that a mobile reader has been tampered with:

  • SDK integration: A TerminalException with TerminalErrorCode READER_TAMPERED
  • Stripe Reader M2: The first and last LEDs flash rapidly, every 0.1 seconds for 30 seconds.
  • BBPOS WisePad 3: A tamper-detected screen error displays and the reader becomes unavailable.

What to do next

The device can’t be reactivated and must be replaced.

  • If under warranty, submit a warranty claim.
  • If purchased through a Connect platform, contact your platform provider.

Help with third-party integrations

Stripe has limited support for issues involving third-party integrations, applications, and plugins. We recommend consulting their documentation if you have questions.

Many third-parties build on top of Stripe, each with their own custom code and unique integrations. Stripe doesn’t build or maintain these integrations, applications, and plugins. When issues arise, we don’t have visibility into their systems or data.

Depending on the type of third-party that you’re reaching out about, Stripe support may or may not be able to assist. See below for the different types of relationships we have with third-parties and to understand the type of support that Stripe can provide.

End-customers

If you’ve received a charge from a merchant that uses Stripe for payment processing, Stripe cannot initiate refunds on behalf of the merchant. To initiate a refund, reach out to the merchant that created the charge. If you have received a charge that’s unfamiliar to you, you can look it up in Stripe’s charge lookup tool.

Stripe connectors

A Stripe connector (or plugin) is an integration between Stripe and a third-party technology platform. There are Stripe owned connectors, like the Stripe Connector for NetSuite,, as well as partner owned connectors. For partner-owned connectors, Stripe doesn’t have visibility and is rarely able to provide support on related issues.

Read more about recommended solutions for Stripe-owned and partner-owned connectors.

Connected accounts

If you’re connected to a third-party platform, see how to get help.

How do I disable Link on my Magento checkout?

Link is a reusable payment method that auto-fills your customers’ payment and shipping details for them at checkout. Customers store their payment information with Link once, and reuse it across all other websites that support it. When new customers come to your site for the first time, they can use Link to pay with their saved payment details.

When Google Pay or Apple Pay are not available on a customer’s device, Link is displayed in their place. Additionally, when the customer is logged into Link from any other website, Link displays with higher priority over other wallets.

If you’d like to disable Link in on your website, you can do so from your Stripe dashboard:

  • For the product pages, minicart, shopping cart, and top checkout section, you can disable it from your Link settings
  • For the redirect flow (Stripe Checkout), you can disable it from your Checkout settings
  • For the embedded flow with Payment Element, you can disable it from your Payment Method settings

Once Link has been disabled, it may take a few minutes for the change to take effect on your website.

How do I resend missed webhooks from Magento?

To re-send / re-play webhooks which were not delivered to your website, you can use one of the following 3 commands:

bin/magento stripe:webhooks:process-event [-f|--force] &lt;event_id>

The above will replay a single webhook event by ID. You can find individual event IDs by navigating to a payment in your Stripe account and scrolling to the bottom of the page where a timeline shows all events. Click on the ‘View event detail’ of an entry to reveal the event ID in the URL bar.

bin/magento stripe:webhooks:process-events-range &lt;from_event_id> &lt;to_event_id>

This will retrieve a list of events, beginning from one event_id until a future event_id, and it will replay all of them. You can select the initial and final event from the Events section of your Stripe Dashboard.

bin/magento stripe:webhooks:process-events-date-range &lt;from_date> &lt;to_date>

This will retrieve a list of events between two dates, and will replay all of them. The date format is arbitrary, you can use strings such as ‘2022-02-15’, ‘yesterday’, ‘now’, ‘10th May 2022’, ‘3 weeks ago’, ‘last Wednesday 15:30’, and so forth.

How do I upgrade my Magento Stripe payments module?

We include instructions outlining how to upgrade your module in our Magento documentation.

There are 2 tabs in this section, the first tab titled ‘From the Marketplace’ is for users who have installed the module from the Magento Marketplace using composer. The second tab, ‘From the raw package’, is for users who have downloaded a binary from stripe.com and extracted it manually in their Magento directory. Please make sure to follow the instructions for the corresponding installation method.

I’m seeing an ‘Invalid webhook signature’ error in Magento

This error means that the signature which has been entered under Stripe → Basic Settings → Webhook Signature is incorrect. When entering a webhook signature, it is important to use the signature for:

  • The correct mode of the module (i.e. Live Mode or Test Mode), and
  • The correct signature for the specific webhook endpoint. If you needed to delete and recreate the webhook endpoint before, then you would also need to update the signature as that may have been changed.

Please note that the webhook signature is optional. Removing it completely is also likely to resolve the problem.

I’m receiving the webhook error ‘origin check failed’ in my Magento dashboard

The webhook ‘origin check failed’ error appears if a webhook event arrives from a webhook endpoint which does not exist in the ‘stripe_webhooks’ table in the database. To resolve this, we recommended that you delete any existing webhook endpoints from the Stripe Dashboard and then re-create them with the following command from your Magento directory:

bin/magento stripe:webhooks:configure

This command will recreate the webhooks and will also save the signing secret for each webhook endpoint in the ‘stripe_webhooks’ database table. If you still see the origin check error after running this command, please check inside var/log/stripe_payments_webhooks.log. In this file, some additional error messages are logged which will explain the reason the origin check failed.

Magento Subscription FAQs

Are subscriptions with bundled products supported in Magento?

Yes, bundled products work with subscriptions.

Can I use Magento’s inventory controls with subscriptions?

Using Magento’s stock control for subscription products isn’t recommended, because if a payment is received and the product is out of stock the order will fail to be created in Magento. If you have another stock control system, it would be best to track the stock separately from your Magento website.

Do Magento subscriptions work with guest customers?

Subscriptions work with guest customers. If a customer registers immediately after placing an order, they will be able to view their subscription from their account. It’s recommended that you encourage them to create an account after creating a subscription so they can manage their subscription going forward.

Is it possible to update the SKU or URL for a subscription in Magento

When a subscription is created in Stripe, the Product ID is saved in that subscription’s metadata. Therefore, changing the SKU or URL will not affect recurring subscriptions.

What happens if I change a subscription’s price in Magento?

If you change a subscription’s price in Magento, when the recurring order is created a Custom Price will be set on that order which will match the original order price. The customer will always be charged the original amount unless you manually migrate the subscription from the CLI to another product that has a different price.

How do Magento customers update expired payment methods for subscriptions?

You can decide what happens when a subscription’s card expires through your Stripe Billing settings. In most cases, you would want Stripe to send a link to the customer through which they can update their card. If they update it through the Stripe hosted page, Magento will automatically reflect the change.

Moving online with platforms and marketplaces powered by Stripe

Stripe partners with thousands of platforms and marketplaces that help businesses move online quickly without any code required. These solutions can help you open up alternative revenue streams and easily reach new or existing customers online to help mitigate the impact of COVID-19 on your business. We’re highlighting some of the most popular apps here, but you can also search for a solution that fits your needs in the Stripe partner directory. PrestaShop

The Stripe Connector for PrestaShop offers a global, flexible, and scalable integrated solution for payments. Companies use this connector to accept payments and build their integration more quickly with PrestaShop and Stripe.

Payment Methods

Does PrestaShop support Link?

Yes, with the latest version of the Stripe module for PrestaShop customers can save their payment details with Link. This can be disabled through the Stripe Dashboard; for the Integrated payment form (Payment Element) here, and for the Redirect to Stripe (Checkout) here.

What payment methods does the Stripe module for PrestaShop support?

The module supports the following payment methods:

  • Credit and debit cards: Visa, Mastercard, American Express, China UnionPay, Discover & Diners, Japan Credit Bureau (JCB), and Cartes Bancaires.
  • Mobile wallets: Apple Pay, Google Pay, WeChat Pay, AliPay, and GrabPay.
  • Buy Now, Pay Later and Installments: Klarna and Afterpay (Clearpay).
  • Bank debits: ACH, SEPA debit, BECS direct debit, and pre-authorized debit in Canada.
  • Other popular payment methods: Bancontact, EPS, Giropay, iDeal, Przelewy24, SOFORT, FPX, Boleto, and OXXO.
How do I configure Apple Pay?

To configure Apple Pay you’ll need to add your domain(s) manually via your Stripe Dashboard in your Payment methods settings.

Configuration

What’s the difference between Checkout and Payment Element?

When configuring the Stripe payment module, you will be able to choose between which Stripe hosted surface we inject into your checkout flow, Redirect to Stripe (Stripe Checkout) or the Integrated payment form (PaymentElement). The primary difference is that with the Payment Element, the element will appear directly in the checkout flow, whereas if you select Checkout the customer will be redirected to Stripe Checkout during the checkout flow.

What are test and live modes?

Test mode allows you to validate that the module works well in your shop and to see what the user experience feels like without actually charging a card or incurring any cost. Once ready to charge your customers with the module, you can switch to live mode. Test and live modes are distinguished by different sets of API keys.

Can I customize the appearance of the checkout?

You can customize the Integrated payment form (Payment Element) to support your checkout context by choosing between four prebuilt themes that most closely resembles your website: Stripe, Flat, Night, None. This can be done from the PrestaShop backoffice on the module configuration page.

To customize the appearance of the checkout when opting to Redirect to Stripe (Stripe Checkout), head to your Branding settings in the Stripe Dashboard.

How do I upgrade my existing Stripe payment module to the newer version?

If there is a newer version of the Stripe module available, you will see an ‘Upgrade’ option beside it in the PrestaShop module manager. The older versions of the Stripe module are fully compatible with the newer version, so you won’t need to make any changes to your configuration when upgrading.

Can I connect to my Stripe account via Oauth?

No, the ‘Connect with Stripe’ button on the module configuration page will only redirect you to the Stripe registration form to fill out with information about your business. To connect, you will still need to use the API keys from your Stripe account.

How do I configure webhooks?

You won’t need to configure webhooks in order for the module to work, this is handled automatically.

Payments and Fees

Are there additional fees when using the Stripe PrestaShop module?

No, the Stripe PrestaShop module does not result in any additional fees. You’re charged standard fees for Stripe’s products as per your account’s pricing.

With separate authorization and capture, can you release an authorized payment from PrestaShop?

No, this has to be done from the Stripe Dashboard.

How do I capture a payment after it has been authorized?

You can configure your payment capture criteria via the PrestaShop backoffice on the Stripe configuration page. The payment capture will be automatically actioned when the order’s status is changed to match the value in the ‘Catch status’ box. You can also capture a payment from the Stripe Dashboard by using the ‘Capture’ button when viewing an authorized payment.

Does PrestaShop support partial refunds?

Yes, you can manually enter the amount you want to refund in the ‘Refund’ tab of the Stripe configuration page. You can also partially refund an order from the Stripe Dashboard.

Product Compatibility

Does PrestaShop support Stripe Billing?

No, the module only supports standalone payments.

Does PrestaShop support Stripe Connect?

Stripe Connect is not supported with the Stripe module for PrestaShop.

Does PrestaShop support Stripe Radar?

Yes, the Stripe module for PrestaShop supports Radar which can be configured from your Stripe Dashboard.

The Refund/Credit Memo email is not being sent from my Magento Dashboard

Under Configuration > Sales > Sales Emails in your Magento Dashboard, you should have the following settings enabled:

Additionally, when you are creating the refund, you need to ensure that the checkbox to ‘Email Copy of Credit Memo’ is ticked.

Setting up your Xero account with Stripe

The Stripe and Xero integration allows users to set up a Stripe account through Xero and attach Stripe as a payment service to Xero invoices. Customers can pay using various payment methods, and Xero will automatically create a spend money transaction for the Stripe fee and mark the invoice as paid. When Stripe transfers the money to the user’s bank account, Xero will automatically find and match all the relevant payments and fees, facilitating a quick and easy reconciliation.

How does the Stripe and Xero integration work?

You would set up a Stripe account through Xero and attach Stripe as a payment service to Xero invoices.

When you send an invoice with Stripe attached, your customer can pay using their credit card or other supported payment methods.

You can choose to cover the Stripe fees or pass them on to your customer (this is known as surcharging).

When the payment is made, Xero will automatically create a spend money transaction for the Stripe fee and mark the invoice as paid.

When Stripe transfers your money to your bank account, Xero will automatically find and match all the relevant payments and fees to complete a quick and easy reconciliation.

I have a Stripe account. How do I connect Stripe and Xero? Do I have to create a new account?

You will be able to connect Xero from your existing Stripe account. Make sure to set up your Stripe account and Xero organization to the correct countries, as you are not able to change these after submission.

To connect your existing Stripe account from the Payment Services Screen within Xero:

  • Make sure you are logged in to Stripe.
  • In Xero, go to Settings > Payment Services > Add Payment Service > select Stripe.
  • Fill in the details in the pop-up (name, credit card logos, payment account, fees).
  • Click Connect to Stripe. You will now be led to the Stripe interface.
  • Select the correct Stripe account you want this Xero organization to be connected to in the dropdown, next to Switch account.
  • Click Connect my Stripe account to complete the connection.

The following article provides more details: central.xero.com

Alternatively, you can refer to this article if you wish to connect an existing Stripe account from an approved invoice: central.xero.com

I do not have a Stripe account. How do I use Stripe with Xero?

From your Xero account:

  • Head to the Organization Menu > Settings > Payment Services > Add Payment Service > select Stripe.
  • Fill in the details in the pop-up (name, credit card logos, payment account, fees).
  • Click Connect to Stripe. You will now be led to the Stripe interface.
  • On the top right corner of the page, click Sign up.
  • Fill in the form to activate your Stripe account. Select the correct country from the dropdown, as you are not able to change the country of your Stripe account once you have submitted this form.
  • Click Authorize access to this account to complete the connection.

The following article provides more details: central.xero.com

Alternatively, please refer to this article if you wish to connect to a new Stripe account from an approved invoice: central.xero.com

When I create an invoice in Xero, I then have to go to Stripe and request the payment. How can I do this automatically when creating an invoice in Xero?

This can happen if your Stripe account is not fully set up and connected

If you have one Stripe account, make sure it has been connected successfully to Xero. In Settings > Payment Services, if there is (pending authentication) next to Stripe, this means that your Stripe account has not been fully set up and connected. Click Edit > Service details and follow the steps to complete your application.

If you have multiple Stripe accounts, make sure you have connected the correct Stripe account to your organization in Xero.

I have set up my account in the wrong country. How can I disconnect Stripe?

To disconnect the Stripe account you set up from Xero, go to Settings > Payment Services > Stripe > Remove.

This also removes it from any invoice branding theme it has been applied to in Xero and therefore, deletes the payment link from the online invoice that uses that branding theme.

I have set up subscriptions in Stripe. Is there a way to set up invoices in Xero and link to my subscriptions in Stripe?

Xero invoicing cannot be used with Stripe subscriptions at this. If you have set up subscriptions in Stripe, the invoices will also have to be handled from within Stripe.

Alternatively, you can also handle subscriptions from Xero by setting up repeating invoices for your customer contacts, and select Stripe as the chosen payment service.

Can I transfer invoices created in Stripe to Xero?

No; there is currently no integration between Stripe invoices and Xero.

Shopware

The Stripe Connector for Shopware 6 offers a global, flexible, and scalable integrated solution for payments. Companies use this connector to accept payments and supercharge their business with Shopware and Stripe.

Payment Methods

Does Shopware support Link?

Yes, Link can be enabled or disabled through the Payment Method settings in the Stripe Dashboard; for the Integrated payment form (Payment Element) here, and for the Redirect to Stripe (Checkout) here.

What Payment Methods does the Stripe module for Shopware support?

The module supports the following Payment Methods:

  • Credit and debit cards: Visa, Mastercard, American Express, China UnionPay, Discover & Diners, Japan Credit Bureau (JCB), and Cartes Bancaires.
  • Mobile wallets: Apple Pay, Google Pay, WeChat Pay, AliPay, and GrabPay.
  • Buy Now, Pay Later and Installments: Klarna and Afterpay (Clearpay).
  • Bank debits: ACH, SEPA debit, BECS direct debit, and pre-authorized debit in Canada.
  • Other popular payment methods: Bancontact, EPS, Giropay, iDeal, Przelewy24, SOFORT, FPX, Boleto, and OXXO.
How do I add or remove payment methods in my payment flow?

This can be done through the Payment Method settings in the Stripe Dashboard.

How do I configure Apple Pay?

To configure Apple Pay you’ll need to add your domain(s) manually via your Stripe Dashboard in your Payment methods settings.

I can only see cards as a payment method in my checkout, but I have activated others.

When you connect your Stripe account to the Stripe Shopware module for the first time through the ‘Connect with Stripe in Live mode’ button, the additional payment methods you’ve enabled become deactivated in your Stripe account. You can turn them on again from the ‘Payment methods’ settings page in your Stripe Dashboard.

Configuration

What’s the difference between Checkout and Payment Element?

When configuring the Stripe payment module, you will be able to choose between which Stripe hosted surface we inject into your checkout flow, Redirect to Stripe (Stripe Checkout) or the Integrated payment form (PaymentElement). The primary difference is that with the PaymentElement, the element will appear directly in the checkout flow, whereas if you select Checkout the customer will be redirected to Stripe Checkout during the checkout flow.

Do I need to configure webhooks?

No, the Stripe module for Shopware 6 works without webhooks.

I’m receiving ‘webhook failed’ emails. What should I do?

If you used the previous Stripe Shopware plugin before transitioning to the app, you might still have an old webhook created and registered. This old webhook doesn’t interfere with the normal functioning of the app, but it may result in you receiving ‘webhook failed’ emails. To stop receiving these emails, follow the steps below:

  • Navigate to the Webhooks section of your Stripe Dashboard.
  • Click on the relevant webhook endpoint URL from the list.
  • Click on the (…) option and choose Delete, then click ‘Delete webhook’ when prompted.
Can I connect to my Stripe account via Oauth?

Yes, you can use the button ‘Connect with Stripe in Live Mode’ to be redirected to Stripe, where you can fill out the form with information about your business, and click ‘Submit’.

What is the difference between ‘Connect with Stripe in Test Mode’ and ‘Connect with Stripe in Live Mode’?

Test mode allows you to validate that the module works well in your shop and to see what the user experience feels like without actually charging a card or incurring any cost. Once ready to charge your customers with the module, you can switch to live mode.

Can I customize the appearance of the checkout?

You can customize the Integrated payment form (Payment Element) to match your checkout context by choosing between four prebuilt themes: Stripe, Flat, Night, None. This can be done from the Shopware backoffice on the module configuration page.

To customize the appearance of the checkout when opting to Redirect to Stripe (Stripe Checkout), head to your Branding settings in the Stripe Dashboard.

I’ve updated the Stripe module, do I need to do anything else?

Yes, after updating the Stripe module you need to add ‘Pay with Stripe’ to the ‘Payment methods’ box in your sales channel again. For example, you can head to ‘Storefront’ in your Shopware backoffice, scroll down to the ‘Payment and shipping’ section, click the arrow next to the ‘Payment methods’ box and then click ‘Pay with Stripe’.

If you want to make Stripe the default payment method, you need to add ‘Pay with Stripe’ to the ‘Default payment method’ box, after which Stripe will be listed first on your checkout page.

Payments and Fees

Can I authorize a payment now and capture it later?

Yes, you can choose between ‘Simultaneous authorization and capture’ and ‘Separate authorization and capture’ on the module configuration page in the Shopware backoffice.

How do I capture a payment after it has been authorized?

To capture an authorized payment, you’ll need to change the order’s ‘Payment status’ from ‘Authorized’ to ‘Paid’ or ‘Partially paid’ in the Shopware backoffice. You can also capture a payment from the Stripe Dashboard, by using the ‘Capture’ when viewing a payment.

How do I refund a payment through Shopware?

To start the refund process, you need to change the order’s status: go to ‘Orders’ -> ‘Overview’ -> click on the order you want to refund (it must be in the ‘Paid’ state) -> change the ‘Payment status’ from ‘Paid’ to ‘Refunded’.

Does Shopware support partial refunds?

No, Shopware doesn’t support partial refunds. The ‘Refunded (partially)’ status will generate a full refund in the same way the ‘Refunded’ status does.

Are there additional fees when using the Stripe Shopware module?

No, the Stripe Shopware module does not result in any additional fees. You’re charged standard fees for Stripe’s products as per your account’s pricing.

Product Compatibility

Does the Stripe Shopware module support recurring payments?

No, it doesn’t support recurring payments or any of Stripe Billing’s functionality.

Does Shopware support Stripe Connect?

Stripe Connect is not supported with the Stripe module for Shopware.

Does Shopware support Stripe Radar?

Yes, the Stripe module for Shopware supports Radar which can be configured from your Stripe Dashboard.

Third-party plugin support for Stripe accounts in India

Stripe supports plug-ins for preview accounts in India. Domestic charges (INR) and export (international) charges (non-INR) are supported with all plug-ins including Shopify, Chargebee, Magento, and WooCommerce.

For domestic transactions, plug-ins should work out of the box.

For export (international) transactions, ensure you follow Indian export requirements. You may wish to reach out to your respective plugin to find out more about supporting Indian export transactions on Stripe if you have more questions.

The webhook endpoint URL in Stripe is different from my store URL in Magento

As long as all store views are hosted on the same Magento instance, then it doesn’t matter which store view is configured in Stripe. The module will accept all webhook events at a single webhook endpoint, and it will load the correct store view based on the order number in the metadata of the webhook event. By default, the Base URL of the Default Store View is configured, which handles events for all child store views.

What kind of refunds can I generate in Magento?

Magento supports 2 types of refunds: Online and Offline. Online refunds will also refund the amount at the payment gateway. Offline refunds will only refund the amount on Magento.

An Offline refund is created when you click the Credit Memo button of the order from the Magento admin area. To perform an Online refund, you need to first find and click on an Invoice and then click the Credit Memo button of the invoice.

We include more details on how this can be done in our Magento documentation.

Why am I seeing incomplete payments in my Stripe Dashboard coming from the Magento module?

In newer versions of the Stripe module for Magento, you will sometimes see incomplete or canceled payments in your Stripe dashboard which have the description “Cart QUOTE_ID”. This is expected behavior.

The reason that these payments are created is because of the transition from the legacy Stripe Elements to the newer PaymentElement. With the new PaymentElement, a PaymentIntent must first be created before the element is displayed. This initial PaymentIntent has an Incomplete status when it is created, and they are not associated with a Magento order yet because an order has not yet been placed.

If the customer does not select Stripe as a payment method, or if they abandon the checkout session, then this will result in a canceled PaymentIntent and a canceled order in Magento.

If they select Stripe, then the payment will be processed and the message will disappear from your Stripe Dashboard. The Magento order will also switch from Pending status to Processing status.

Treasury

EU payment methods for funding your business account

Your EU business account holds euros and can receive funds via two SEPA payment methods: SEPA Credit Transfer for standard next-business-day transfers, and SEPA Instant for transfers that arrive within seconds. Both are push-only and use the same account details - the IBAN and BIC found in the Stripe Dashboard under Financial account > Account details.

SEPA (Single Euro Payments Area) is the European framework that standardizes EUR transfers across 36 countries, making a payment from a German bank to a Spanish bank as straightforward as a domestic transfer.

SEPA Credit Transfer

SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) is the standard euro transfer mechanism used across Europe. The sender enters your IBAN and BIC at their bank, and the payment arrives in your Stripe business account the next SEPA business day.

SEPA processes on business days only, following the TARGET2 calendar maintained by the European Central Bank. It doesn’t run on weekends or certain European public holidays. A transfer sent on a Friday settles the following Monday.

There is no practical per-transaction cap, making SEPA Credit Transfer the right choice for large EUR amounts.

Best for: Standard euro top-ups on business days; amounts above 1 million EUR. Free to receive.

SEPA Instant

SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) is the real-time version of SEPA. Payments arrive within 10 seconds, at any time of day, every day of the year, including weekends and holidays when standard SEPA doesn’t process. It uses the same IBAN and BIC as a standard SEPA transfer; the sender selects the instant option (labelled variously as “instant payment”, “Sofort-Überweisung”, “virement instantané”, or similar depending on the bank and country).

There is a scheme cap of 1 million EUR per transaction. For amounts above this, use SEPA Credit Transfer instead.

Availability depends on whether the sender’s bank supports outbound SEPA Instant. Adoption has grown significantly across the EU, but not all banks offer it. If your sender doesn’t have the option, a standard SEPA Credit Transfer will still arrive the next business day.

Best for: Urgent EUR funding; transfers outside SEPA business hours; amounts up to 1 million EUR. Free to receive.

Funding your financial account

You can add funds to your financial account by transferring from your payments balance or from an external bank account. Transfers from your payments balance are instant, while external funding times vary. Read more about adding money to a financial account.

How do I add funds to my financial account, and how long does it take?

Add funds to your financial account in one of three ways:

Transfer from your payments balance

This method is instant and free.

  • Navigate to the Balances page in your Stripe Dashboard.
  • Click Transfer > Transfer and convert funds.
  • Select Payments Balance as source and select the financial account to add money to.
  • Enter the amount, review, and confirm.
External funding - credit transfer (push)

Timing varies from instant to 5 business days, depending on your risk profile and transfer method.

  • In your Dashboard, click Add Funds > External Bank transfer.
  • Use the provided Stripe bank details to transfer funds from your bank.
External funding - debit transfer (pull - US only)

This method typically takes 3-5 business days.

  • In your Dashboard, click Add Funds > Stripe Initiated Debit.
  • Select amount, bank account to debit, and the financial account to add money to.
  • Confirm the transfer.

I added funds to my financial account but don’t see them. Where did that money go?

If you’ve added funds to your financial account and they’re not showing up:

  • Verify your funding method: payments balance funding, debit, or credit transfer.
For funding from your payments balance
  • Ensure you have enough funds in your payments balance.
  • If you have enough funds in your balance, take a screenshot of your balance or error message and contact Stripe Support.
For credit transfers
  • If you initiated the transfer recently, wait a few days as processing times can vary.
  • Double-check that the bank details are correct.
  • Contact your bank about the status of the transfer.
  • If your bank confirms the transfer was successful, contact Stripe Support with proof of transfer.
For debits
  • If you initiated the transfer recently, wait a few days as processing times can vary.
  • Contact your bank about the status of the debit.
  • If your bank confirms the transfer was successful, contact Stripe Support with proof of debit.

I have transferred funds (InboundTransfer) to my financial account. How can I cancel it?

Inbound Transfers can only be canceled if it is still being processed and funds have yet to land in your financial account. Once the InboundTransfer has succeeded, it is no longer possible to be canceled.

Alternatively, you can also create an OutboundTransfer, to send funds out from your financial account, to your external bank account.

How can I set up recurring funding to my financial account?

To set up recurring funding, use the revenue splitting feature in your Stripe Dashboard:

  • Go to Settings in your Stripe Dashboard.
  • Navigate to Bank accounts and currencies.
  • Select Set up recurring transfers.

From here, you can configure recurring transfers from your payments balance to your financial account.

To use this feature, you need to be on an automatic payout schedule. Then select from the following:

  • Transfer a target amount
  • Transfer all of your payments balance
  • Don’t transfer any of your payments balance

Read more about how to transfer funds from your Stripe balance.

My financial account balance is negative. What can I do?

You may begin to receive periodic reminder emails if your financial account’s negative balance persists.

Add funds to your financial account immediately to cover the negative balance. Adding funds promptly helps prevent service interruptions.

Use one of the methods mentioned above:

  • Transfer from your payments balance
  • External funding - credit transfer (push)
  • External funding - debit transfer (pull - US only)

Funding your UK business account

Your UK business account holds GBP and can receive funds via two methods: Faster Payments and CHAPS. Both are initiated by you from your external bank account. For more details on how each payment method works, see UK payment methods for funding your business account.

Finding your UK business account details

  • In the Stripe Dashboard, go to Balances > Business account.
  • Select Account details.
  • You will see your sort code (6 digits, format: XX-XX-XX) and account number (8 digits), as well as a Bank Identifier Code (BIC) and International Bank Account Number (IBAN) for international payments.

Share these details with any bank sending you funds. They appear as standard UK account details to the sender.

FAQ

Does Stripe charge a fee for receiving FPS or CHAPS payments?

Stripe doesn’t charge a fee to receive FPS or CHAPS payments into your business account. Your sending bank may charge a fee for outbound CHAPS transfers; check with your bank.

How do I know if my payment has arrived?

You’ll see it reflected in your Stripe business account balance in the Dashboard. You can also set up balance notifications in Dashboard settings.

What happens if I send a CHAPS payment after the cutoff?

Your bank will typically reject the payment or hold it until the next business day. Contact your bank directly to confirm their handling of after-hours CHAPS submissions.

Can I receive payments in currencies other than GBP?

Your UK business account holds GBP. Payments sent in a foreign currency will either be rejected or converted depending on the sending bank’s behavior. To receive EUR, use your EU business account and SEPA.

My FPS payment hasn’t arrived after 30 minutes. What should I do?

FPS is typically instant but can occasionally be delayed by the sending bank’s processing. Check with your sending bank first. If the payment was confirmed as sent and has not arrived after 2 hours, contact Stripe support with the payment reference from your bank.

Can I receive international wires?

Your business account supports international wires using Swift.

To send a transfer, enter the BIC and IBAN in your banking application. Choose to pay all transfer fees yourself so the full amount reaches your account. Your bank may label this option “OUR”.

If you choose a different fee option, fees will reduce the amount received. Your business account accepts Swift transfers in GBP only.

Funding your US financial account

Top up your US financial account by pulling funds from a linked bank account, or pushing funds from your external bank. For details on how each payment method works, see US payment methods for funding your financial accounts.

Initiating a top-up

Pull from external bank (ACH Debit)
  • Go to Balances > Financial account in the Dashboard.
  • Select Add money > Linked bank account.
  • Choose your verified external bank account. If you haven’t verified your bank account, you’ll need to complete microdeposit verification or add your bank account again by logging in through Financial Connections.
  • Enter the amount and confirm.

Stripe initiates the ACH debit on the next business day. Funds typically arrive in 0-3 business days.

Push from your bank (ACH Credit, Fedwire or RTP)

No setup is required in Stripe. Instruct your external bank to send a payment to:

  • Routing number: found in the Dashboard under Financial account > Account details
  • Account number: found in the same location
  • Account holder name: your business name as registered with Stripe

ACH Credit funds typically arrive in 1–2 business days. For same-day settlement, use Fedwire and ensure your bank submits the wire before 5pm ET on a business day. Alternatively, use RTP, which is available 24/7.
