FAQ

Do ACH transfers have a minimum or maximum?

There is no Stripe-imposed minimum. ACH transfers are subject to your bank’s per-transaction limits, and Stripe may apply daily or monthly limits based on your account type. Contact support if you need higher limits.

Why hasn’t my ACH pull arrived after 5 business days?

ACH returns can occur if there are insufficient funds, the account is closed, or the account holder disputes the debit. Check the Dashboard under Financial account > Transactions for any return codes. If no return is shown and it has been more than 5 business days, contact Stripe support.

Can I cancel an ACH Debit pull after initiating it?

ACH Debit pulls can be cancelled within a short window (typically same day) before they’re submitted to the network. After submission, cancellation isn’t possible; you’d need to wait for settlement and then move the funds back.

What are the Fedwire routing details?

Your financial account’s routing number and account number for Fedwire are the same as for ACH. Both are visible in the Dashboard under Financial account > Account details.

Get started with stablecoins using Stripe Treasury

Treasury with a stablecoin balance is a business account built directly into your Stripe Dashboard, designed for entrepreneurs who operate across borders.

With a stablecoin balance you can:

  • Send and receive USD stablecoins instantly, from anywhere in the world over nine networks
  • Create physical and virtual cards for your business
  • Send and receive USD through ACH transfers and domestic wires, and EUR over SEPA
  • Pay and get paid with low foreign exchange (FX) fees

Eligible businesses can use Stripe Treasury to hold and manage a stablecoin balance. How you get started depends on whether your business incorporated through Stripe Atlas.

If your business incorporated through Stripe Atlas

  • If you haven’t already, register and submit an Atlas application to incorporate your company. See our docs for more information and detailed registration instructions.
  • Once your Atlas company has been incorporated, visit the Atlas overview page in your Dashboard.
  • Expand Get a business account to manage your money under the Next steps header. From here, you can compare banking options and get started with Stripe Treasury.
  • Provide your personal identification details to verify your identity and set up two-step authentication to secure your account when prompted.
    • If your business has multiple beneficial owners, you will be asked to provide identity details for each owner.
  • You’ll see a new USD Stablecoin balance on the Balances page of your Dashboard. It may take a few minutes for us to set up your account details. You’ll receive an email when it’s complete.

If your business didn’t incorporate through Stripe Atlas

  • If you have not already onboarded to Stripe Treasury, you can do so by navigating to the Treasury page in the Stripe Dashboard.
  • If you are already using Stripe Treasury and wish to add a stablecoin balance, you can do so from the Balances page in the Stripe Dashboard.

Using your stablecoin business account

  • Add funds to your USD Stablecoin balance via bank or crypto transfer:
    • Add from a bank account
      • On the Balances overview, click Add funds.
      • Click Bank transfer.
      • Copy the required account information, then complete the transfer through your bank.
    • Add from a crypto wallet
      • On the Balances overview, click Add funds.
      • Click Crypto transfer.
      • Select a crypto network.
      • Copy the wallet address or scan the QR code with your crypto wallet.
      • Click Done.
  • Create a card and add it to your Apple or Google Wallet. You can find more information on stablecoin-backed cards and steps to create a card.
    • Stablecoin cards within Stripe Treasury are available only for Stripe Atlas accounts owned by founders outside the United States.
    • If your account is based in the United States, newly issued cards will use your USD balance. You can’t choose a stablecoin balance as the funding source.

See our Stablecoins Docs to learn more.

Instant currency conversion

With instant currency conversion, you can convert funds between currencies directly from your Stripe Dashboard. This is available for funds in both your payments balance and your business or checking account. A conversion fee applies, included in the exchange rate shown at the time of conversion.

How to convert funds

  • Go to the Balances page, then click Convert.
  • On the conversion details page, select the currencies to convert and enter the amount.
  • Click Submit. You’ll see the funds instantly available in your balance.

Converted funds appear in the target currency balance immediately and will pay out on your normal schedule.

For supported currencies by region, see instant currency conversion documentation.

Common scenarios

I have a balance but no bank account in that currency

If you have funds in a currency but no bank account set up to receive payouts in that currency, your balance won’t pay out automatically. This can happen if you removed a bank account or settlement currency

How to fix it:

  • Option 1 (recommended): Convert the balance to a currency where you already have a bank account using the steps above. The funds will pay out on your normal schedule.
  • Option 2: Add a bank account in that currency via Settings > Bank accounts and scheduling.
My balance is below the minimum payout threshold

Some currencies have a minimum payout amount when using multi-currency settlement. If your balance is below this threshold, Stripe won’t automatically send a payout.

This typically happens when you have a small remaining balance from old transactions and you’re no longer actively receiving payments in that currency.

How to fix it:

Convert the balance to your primary settlement currency using instant currency conversion. Once converted, the funds are combined with your existing balance and will pay out normally.

Example: You have $48 USD sitting in your account with a $250 threshold. Your primary currency is CAD. Convert the $48 USD to CAD, and it will be paid out with your next regular CAD payout.

Other options:

  • Wait for more payments in that currency until the balance reaches the minimum.
  • Add a bank account in a region with a lower threshold for that currency.
I need to cover a negative balance in another currency

If a refund or chargeback created a negative balance in one currency but you have a positive balance in another, you can convert funds to cover it:

  • Go to Balances in the Dashboard
  • Click Convert next to the currency with a positive balance
  • Select the currency with the negative balance as the target
  • Convert enough to cover the negative amount
  • Confirm the conversion

The converted funds will be applied to your negative balance immediately.

Example: You issued a USD refund but your USD balance is -50. You have GBP 200 GBP. Convert enough GBP to USD to cover the USD -50, and the pending refund will go through.

If you don’t have a positive balance in another currency, the negative will be covered by future incoming payments or auto-debit from your bank account. See Fix the negative balance on your account

I’m closing my account and have small balances in multiple currencies

If you want to withdraw all funds before closing your account, convert all small balances into one currency first. This ensures you can withdraw everything in a single payout without being blocked by minimum thresholds.

Troubleshooting

I can’t see the Convert button
  • Instant currency conversion may not be available in your country yet. Check the supported regions.
  • It’s only available for users with Dashboard access.
I just topped up my payments balance but can’t convert it

Top-up funds are not eligible for instant currency conversion. Only funds that arrived through payment processing (charges, transfers from platforms, etc.) can be converted. This does not apply to Treasury.

The conversion rate seems different from what I expected

Stripe applies the mid-market rate based on pricing data from third-party service providers. This ensures that you’re getting a competitive and fair exchange rate for your currency conversions.

I accidentally completed a currency conversion exchange. Can I cancel or convert back without incurring FX fees again?

No, conversions cannot be cancelled once confirmed. The process is instant. If you need to convert back to the original currency, you’ll need to initiate a new conversion, which will be subject to the standard conversion fee again.

Settlement pauses FAQ

This FAQ applies to Stripe accounts where payment proceeds settle into a default business account that also supports eligible money-management features.

A settlement pause temporarily holds affected payment proceeds in a settlement reserve instead of adding them to your available balance. This includes new payments and payment funds that are still pending. You can continue accepting payments, and funds that were already available aren’t automatically held. If Stripe needs information from you, you’ll see a task or notification in the Stripe Dashboard.

Any other restrictions on your account apply separately and will be shown in the Dashboard.

What is a settlement pause?

A settlement pause temporarily directs affected payment proceeds, including new payment funds and payment funds that are still pending, to a reserved balance until the underlying issue is resolved. Funds in the settlement reserve aren’t available for payouts or other money movement until they’re released.

A settlement pause doesn’t hold funds that were already in your available balance or stop you from accepting new payments. But instead it pauses incoming payments only and allows you to still use funds already settled in your account.

Why was a settlement pause placed on my account?

Stripe may place a settlement pause when an issue must be resolved before affected payment proceeds can be added to your available balance. Check your Stripe Dashboard and communications from Stripe for information about the restriction and any action you need to take.

A settlement pause holds affected payment proceeds without restricting funds that were already available.

What funds are affected by a settlement pause?

A settlement pause applies to affected proceeds from payments that are new or still pending when the pause starts. Those proceeds may be placed in the settlement reserve.

Funds that were already available before the pause aren’t automatically moved into the settlement reserve.

Can I continue accepting payments?

Yes. A settlement pause itself doesn’t prevent you from accepting payments. While it is active, affected payment proceeds will be added to the settlement reserve instead of your available balance.

If a separate restriction affects your ability to accept payments, it will be shown separately in the Dashboard.

Can I still make payouts or use my available balance?

The settlement pause itself doesn’t block funds that are already shown as available. You can continue using those available funds for payouts or other supported money movement unless a separate restriction applies.

Funds shown in the settlement reserve can’t be paid out or otherwise used until they’re released. Separate account restrictions may also affect how you can use your available balance.

How can I resolve a settlement pause?

  • Open the settlement-pause notice in the Stripe Dashboard or check the Account status page under Settings.
  • Select View task if that option appears.
  • Provide all requested information and submit the task.
  • Monitor the Dashboard and email for updates or additional requests.

If no task is shown, contact Stripe Support to confirm whether any action is required.

I completed the task. Why is the settlement pause still active?

Submitting a task doesn’t always remove the settlement pause immediately. Stripe may need time to review the information you provided. An active pause after submission doesn’t necessarily mean that your submission was unsuccessful.

Monitor the Dashboard and email for the outcome or for any request for more information.

How long will the settlement pause remain in place?

A settlement pause doesn’t have a standard scheduled expiration date. It remains active until the related review or requirement is resolved.

Complete any task in the Dashboard and check the Dashboard or Stripe communications for the current status.

When will my reserved funds be released?

Once the settlement pause is lifted, the affected funds are released from the settlement reserve to your regular balance. The funds keep their original payment-availability timing: funds whose normal availability date has passed can become available, while funds with a future availability date remain pending until that date. Any separate account restrictions still apply.

Stripe Support can’t promise a release date before the review is complete.

How is a settlement pause different from a payout pause?

A settlement pause affects new payment proceeds before they’re added to your available balance. Funds that were already available aren’t automatically blocked.

A payout pause prevents funds from being paid out. It can therefore affect funds that are already available. If both controls apply to your account, the Dashboard will show the relevant restrictions.

What should I do if I don’t see a task or need more help?

Check the Dashboard account status, balance details, and recent communications from Stripe. If you don’t see a required action, contact Stripe Support to confirm whether Stripe needs anything from you.

How do refunds and disputes affect funds in the settlement reserve?

Refunds and disputes continue to be processed while a settlement pause is active. When a refund or dispute relates to a payment whose proceeds are held in the settlement reserve, eligible held funds are released to help cover that refund or dispute. Any remaining funds stay reserved until they’re otherwise released. Currently, a full refund or dispute triggers release of the corresponding reserve hold. Partial refunds and disputes don’t yet trigger a proportional release.

Can I appeal a settlement pause?

You can ask Stripe to review the settlement pause. Complete any requested task in the Stripe Dashboard and provide the requested information. If no task is available, or if you believe the pause was applied incorrectly, contact Stripe Support. Stripe will route the request to the team responsible for the restriction. Submitting information or requesting a review doesn’t guarantee that the pause will be removed immediately. Other restrictions may also remain in place.

Treasury account availability for Stripe Atlas businesses

Stripe Atlas businesses may be eligible for Treasury accounts that hold US dollars (USD), stablecoins (OUSD or USDC), or both. Availability depends on the physical location of your account representative and the address information provided for your business and its owners.

All Atlas businesses are registered in the United States. However, US incorporation alone doesn’t determine which Treasury account you can access.

Atlas businesses whose account representative has a physical address in the United States may be eligible for a Treasury account that holds funds in USD.

Your representative’s address must reflect their actual physical location. A US registered-agent or virtual mailing address doesn’t establish that your representative is physically located in the United States.

Can I transfer money to and from external bank accounts with a stablecoin Treasury account?

Yes. A stablecoin Treasury account still provides USD account and routing numbers for receiving supported bank transfers, and supports transfers out to external bank accounts.

The distinction is how your balance is held: having USD account and routing numbers doesn’t mean your Treasury balance is held in USD. Your stablecoin Treasury balance is held in OUSD or USDC.

Use the transfer instructions shown in your Stripe Dashboard for the supported transfer methods and required account details.

Treasury direct debits

A direct debit is an ACH payment that an external party—such as a payroll provider, supplier, or tax authority—pulls from your Stripe financial account using its account and routing numbers. The external party initiates the collection; adding a vendor in the Stripe Dashboard doesn’t send a payment.

Direct debits are available for eligible Treasury direct business accounts in the United States and use USD. This is different from using ACH debit to add money to your financial account from an external bank account.

For more information, see Treasury direct debits.

Enable or disable direct debits

Direct debit settings apply separately to each financial account.

  • In the Stripe Dashboard, open Balances.
  • Select the relevant financial account and its USD balance.
  • Select More, then ACH direct debits.
  • Turn Allow ACH debits from the selected account (USD) on or off.
  • Select Save. If you are turning debits off, review the confirmation and select Turn off.

Turning direct debits off blocks upcoming and scheduled collections from all vendors for that financial account, including legitimate collections. Your saved vendors and limits remain available if you turn direct debits on again.

Turning direct debits off doesn’t return a debit that has already settled or cancel an agreement with a vendor. Contact the vendor separately to cancel the underlying bill, subscription, or collection arrangement.

Manage vendor authorizations

You can manage vendors under ACH direct debits > Vendor list. The vendor’s ACH Company ID identifies the party originating the collection. Ask the vendor to confirm its Company ID if you don’t know it.

Choose the option that matches how you want the account to work:

  • Approve listed vendors: Only vendors with a matching active authorization can debit the financial account. If the approved-vendor list is empty, no vendors match.
  • Set debit limits for listed vendors: Vendors that are not listed can still debit the account, subject to the default limit and other checks. Listed vendors can have their own limits.

Adding a vendor doesn’t automatically restrict the account to approved vendors. Removing a vendor also doesn’t block that vendor when authorizations are optional.

Set debit limits

The standard default is 50,000 USD per debit. You can set a different default of up to 500,000 USD per debit in the Dashboard.

A vendor-specific limit takes precedence over the financial-account default, whether it’s higher or lower. If a vendor doesn’t have its own limit, the financial-account default applies.

These limits apply to each debit, not to a daily or monthly total. Available funds and other account checks still apply.

Troubleshoot a rejected or missing direct debit

If a vendor says that a direct debit was rejected, review:

  • Whether direct debits were enabled for the affected financial account when the vendor attempted the collection
  • Whether vendor authorizations are required
  • Whether the authorization uses the vendor’s correct ACH Company ID
  • The vendor-specific and financial-account limits
  • Whether sufficient funds were available when the collection was processed
  • Any recent changes to the account’s direct debit settings

Changing a setting doesn’t retry a failed collection. After resolving the issue, coordinate any new collection attempt directly with the vendor.

If the settings don’t explain the rejection, the transaction is missing, or your balance appears incorrect, contact Stripe Support. Include the vendor, amount, attempted date and time, visible error, and transaction ID if available. You don’t need a transaction ID to ask us to investigate a missing collection.

Dispute an unrecognized direct debit

If you don’t recognize a settled direct debit:

  • Open Balances in the Stripe Dashboard.
  • Select the relevant financial account and its USD balance.
  • Open the debit from Recent activity or View more.
  • Review the amount, date, vendor information, ACH Company ID, and Disputable until timestamp.
  • If Dispute is available, select it, review the details, and submit the dispute immediately.

The dispute period is one business day from settlement. Always use the Disputable until timestamp shown on the transaction. If Dispute remains available, submit the dispute immediately even if more than one business day has elapsed.

After submission, open the original debit and select View dispute to track the request. Submitting a dispute doesn’t guarantee that the return will succeed.

If the deadline has passed, the Dispute action is missing before the displayed deadline, or the submission fails, contact Stripe Support immediately. Include the amount, date, vendor information, transaction ID if available, displayed deadline or error, and why you believe the debit was unauthorized or incorrect.

Track a dispute

Open the original debit and select View dispute:

  • Submitted: The request is processing, typically for a few business days. This doesn’t mean the return has succeeded.
  • Succeeded: The return succeeded. Check the activity and balance of the financial account linked to the original debit for the returned funds.
  • Failed: Contact Stripe Support so we can review the failure and determine whether any further action is available.

Contact Stripe Support if a dispute remains submitted longer than expected, succeeds without a visible credit, or fails. Include the original debit and dispute IDs if they are available and a screenshot of the relevant status or account activity.

Fees

Stripe doesn’t charge a per-transaction fee for a direct debit or for disputing a direct debit on your Stripe Treasury account. This doesn’t mean that every Treasury product or vendor charge is free.

If you see an unexplained charge, contact Stripe Support and include the line-item description.

Treasury Fee Credit Rewards

If you use Treasury in the US or Australia (in Private Preview), you can earn annual fee credits equal to 1% of your financial account balance when you hold more than 2,000 USD / USDC / AUD. Stripe automatically applies these credits to eligible fees.

You can find out more on how fee credit rewards work.

Which markets is this available in?

This is available to all US-based direct Treasury users, and is in private preview for AU direct Treasury users.

Do I need to enroll into this?

There is no separate enrollment step. All eligible US / AU direct Treasury users are enrolled automatically.

Can fee credits be withdrawn, transferred, or converted to cash?

No. Fee credits are cashless, account-specific, non-refundable, and non-transferable. Stripe applies credits automatically according to eligibility.

Which fees can the credits be used to offset?

You can apply Stripe fee credits to most Stripe fees. In the Stripe Dashboard, you can see which Stripe fees are eligible for each credit on the credit details page.

Some fees aren’t enabled by default due to how they’re charged. For credits to apply to fees such as blended card payments or local payment method payments, you have to change the way these fees are charged and opt in to standalone fees.

What changes when I opt in to standalone fees?

Standalone fees provide an alternative method for Stripe to apply its transaction fees. When you opt in to standalone fees, you will receive the full payment amount instead of a payment net of its fees, and Stripe will post the fee separately (typically within 36 hours).

For example:

  • Inline fees: For a 100 USD transaction with a 3 USD Stripe fee, you receive 97 USD immediately, with a 3 USD fee applied in real time.
  • Standalone fees: For the same 100 USD transaction and 3 USD Stripe fee, you initially receive the full 100 USD. We then apply the 3 USD fee to your account balance later, typically within the next 36 hours.

This can change transaction details, Dashboard exports, Balance Transactions API data, and custom reconciliation. To view and reconcile fee credits, use the All fees report as your primary source for fee reporting.

When will my fee credits be issued?

Rewards calculated during the current month will be credited in the beginning of the following month

Where can I see my fee credits?

You can view issued credits, remaining amounts, usage, and expiration dates in the Dashboard under Settings → Plans and fees → Fee credits. .

Will fee credits expire?

Yes. Fee credits will expire 12 months after they are issued.

What happens when a credit expires or is insufficient?

Once fee credits expires after 12 months or is depleted, eligible fees return to the normal payment method (usually the Stripe balance). If a credit covers only part of a fee, the remainder will be covered by the Stripe balance.

The All fees report will provide the clearest unified view of these split payments.

Treasury: Eligibility and onboarding

Stripe Treasury is being gradually rolled out to eligible users in the US, UK, EU and Australia. Here’s what you need to know about onboarding and eligibility.

How do I know if I’m eligible to use Treasury?

Eligible users will receive an email and an in-dashboard notification when their account receives access to Treasury. If you haven’t received this notification, you’re not currently eligible.

I have multiple Stripe accounts, and one is eligible and the others are not.

Eligibility is determined on an account-by-account basis. It’s possible for one of your Stripe accounts to be eligible while others aren’t. Differences in account details and the timing of our phased rollout can affect eligibility. Check your email and the Stripe Dashboard for updates.

What kind of information do I need to provide for onboarding?

For most users, onboarding is automatic. In some cases, we’ll ask for additional information about your business, its owners, or its representatives to meet financial regulations. If we need anything from you, you’ll see a prompt when you activate Treasury.

I was notified that I’m not eligible for Treasury. Can I appeal this decision?

Unfortunately, we cannot accept appeals for our eligibility decisions.

Why am I not eligible for Treasury?

Eligibility is determined separately for each Stripe account. Your account might not be eligible for Treasury if:

• We need more information to verify your business, its owners, or its representatives.

• For US-based accounts, your business or representative doesn’t meet the location or physical-presence requirements.

• Your account has restrictions or outstanding risk or compliance requirements.

• Your business type or activity isn’t supported.

• Your account setup or use of other Stripe products isn’t currently compatible with Treasury.

• Treasury hasn’t been made available to your account yet.

Eligibility can change over time. If your account becomes eligible, we’ll notify you by email and in the Stripe Dashboard.

Treasury: FAQ

What is Stripe Treasury and how does it differ from the payments balance?

Your payments balance lets you collect payments from customers and pay them out to an external bank account. Treasury is a more comprehensive money management solution that lets you:

  • Create a financial account
  • Receive, store, and manage funds within a single integrated platform
  • Store balances in multiple currencies
  • Send money domestically and internationally to third parties (Global Payouts)
  • Create virtual and physical cards for business spending
  • Perform currency conversions with transparent fee information

Can a vendor debit my Stripe financial account?

Yes. An authorized third party can use the account and routing numbers for an eligible US Treasury Direct business account to initiate a direct debit. You can manage direct debit availability, vendor authorizations, and per-debit limits from Balances > Relevant financial account > USD > More > ACH direct debits.

If you do not recognize a settled debit, open it from the financial account’s activity and submit a dispute immediately if Dispute is available. If the dispute window has passed, contact Stripe Support.

How many financial accounts can I have?

You can have one financial account per Stripe account.

How do I delete my financial account?

If you’d like to delete your financial account, reach out to Stripe Support.

Is there a limit on the amount of funds I can store or how long I can store them?

There are no limits on the funds you can store in your financial account or how long you can keep them there.

How are my funds protected? Is the money I store on Stripe insured?

Fund protection depends on your location:

  • United States: USD funds in your financial account are FDIC insured up to 250,000 USD.
  • United Kingdom: Funds are safeguarded under Stripe’s obligations as an E-Money Institution, meaning they’re protected through segregation and ringfencing practices. Read more about fund safeguarding in the UK.

Can I earn interest on money stored in a financial account?

Stripe doesn’t offer interest or yield on financial account balances.

Treasury: Transfers

You can transfer money from your business or checking accounts to your external bank account. There’s no fee to transfer funds to your bank accounts that are linked to your Stripe account. Read more about transferring money to a external account.

Is there a limit on the amount I can transfer to my external bank account?

Yes. Limits vary depending on the country and the payment rail used.

Minimum Payout Amount for US: 0.01 USD

Maximum Payout Amounts for US:

  • Wire: 10,000,000 USD
  • Standard: 1,000,000 USD
  • Instant: 9,999 USD

Minimum Payout Amount for UK: 0.01 GBP, 0.01 EUR, 0.01 USD

Maximum Payout Amounts for UK:

  • Standard GBP: 1,000,000 GBP
  • Standard USD: 1,000,000 USD

Read more about country-specific payout amounts.

My transfer failed. What can I do?

If your transfer failed, first check the reason for the failure in your Stripe Dashboard. Failures often happen due to incorrect bank details. After addressing the issue, you can initiate the transfer again. If problems persist, contact Stripe Support for assistance.

I haven’t received my transfer yet. What can I do?

  • Check the status of the transfer in your Stripe Dashboard
  • If the status is Paid or Posted, the payment has been sent to your bank
  • Contact your bank and provide them with the Trace ID (available in your Stripe Dashboard)
  • If your bank can’t locate the payment, ask for a written statement confirming this
  • Contact Stripe Support with this statement for further assistance

Can I reverse an transfer?

If you believe a reversal is necessary - either due to a mistaken transfer or suspected fraudulent activity - you can request a reversal by contacting Stripe Support. Stripe will attempt to reverse the outbound payment or transfer and return the funds to your account, however, Stripe can’t guarantee the success of the reversal.

UK payment methods for funding your business account

Your UK business account holds GBP and can receive funds via two networks: Faster Payments for near-instant everyday transfers, and CHAPS for same-day high-value payments. Both use the same account details, which you can find in the Stripe Dashboard under Business account > Account details.

Faster Payments

Faster Payments (FPS) is the UK’s everyday payment network, used for the vast majority of personal and business bank transfers. It’s what happens behind the scenes when you send money via your UK banking app.

Faster Payments operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with no cutoff times and no bank holiday restrictions. Most UK banks include it at no charge.

The scheme allows payments up to 1,000,000 GBP, but many banks apply their own lower per-transaction limits (often 25,000-250,000 GBP for retail and business accounts). If your sender’s bank limit is lower than the amount you need, CHAPS is the alternative.

Best for: Day-to-day top-ups at any time, any day. Free to receive.

CHAPS

CHAPS (Clearing House Automated Payment System) is the UK’s high-value same-day payment system, operated by the Bank of England. Each payment settles individually and is final once processed. It’s the system used for property purchases, large corporate transactions, and any transfer where same-day certainty and no upper limit matter.

CHAPS operates on UK business days only. Your sending bank will have a daily submission cutoff, typically around 3pm GMT/BST, though some banks cut off as early as 2:30pm. Payments submitted after the cutoff are held until the next business day. Your sending bank will usually charge an outbound fee of 15-40 GBP.

Best for: Large transfers that exceed your sender’s Faster Payments limit, or when same-day settlement on a business day is required. No upper limit.

Swift

Swift is a secure messaging service that banks use to send international payments. Swift operates during regular banking hours. There are no transaction limits for international wires, but Swift payments typically take 1-5 business days to arrive. Your bank will likely charge a fee.

Your UK business account accepts Swift transfers only in GBP.

Best for: High-value, international transfers. Free to receive.

Understanding your default business account

A default business account brings payment settlement and eligible Stripe Treasury money-management features together in one place.

Proceeds from your Stripe payments settle directly into this account. The way Stripe processes payments, refunds, disputes, and payouts doesn’t change. Your default business account also gives you access to additional ways to manage and use your money, depending on the features available to you.

Who can use a default business account?

Stripe is gradually rolling out default business accounts to eligible Stripe users in the United States. Not every US account has access at this time.

Stripe will inform you if a default business account becomes available for your account. You can view and manage your default business account from the Balances page in the Stripe Dashboard.

If you haven’t received a notification and don’t see a default business account in the Dashboard, continue using your existing payments balance and the options displayed in the Dashboard.

How does a default business account work?

Your default business account is where proceeds from your Stripe payments settle. Refunds, disputes, and payouts are also reflected in and handled through this account. Once your payment proceeds are available, you can use them with the eligible money-management features shown in the Dashboard.

What changes?

Instead of seeing a separate payments balance, you’ll see a business account marked Default. Proceeds from your Stripe payments settle into this account.

Once payment funds become available, you can use them with the features supported by your account without first moving them to another financial account.

What stays the same?

Nothing changes about how you accept payments or how Stripe processes them:

  • Payment authorization, capture, and processing continue to work as before.
  • Payment proceeds follow the same pending and available balance timelines.
  • You can continue creating refunds and responding to disputes as you do today. Refunds, disputes, and related balance activity appear in your default business account.
  • You can continue making payouts from your available balance through the existing payout process.

What additional features might be available?

Your default business account might support additional Stripe Treasury features. The Dashboard shows which features are available to your account.

To find them, open the Balances page and select your default business account. The available actions and money-management options appear with the account.

You might be able to:

  • Add money: Open your default business account to view its account details and available funding methods. You can use those account details to send money from an external bank through a supported credit transfer. You might also be able to initiate a debit transfer from a linked external bank account.
  • Send money to third parties: View the available sending options for your default business account and pay another person or business—for example, to pay a bill—without first paying the funds out to your own bank account.
  • Convert currencies: View, hold, and convert funds in supported currencies using the currency options shown for your account.
  • Create additional business accounts: Create separate business accounts to organize funds for different purposes.
  • Create a checking account: If available to you, create a checking account with its own features and terms. Checking accounts are a separate account type from business accounts.
  • Create cards: If available to your account, create and manage Stripe-issued cards that spend from your default business account.
  • Transfer money to your own bank: Continue creating payouts from your available balance through the existing Dashboard flow or API.

Available transfer methods, currencies, processing times, and account features can vary. Check the Dashboard to confirm what your account supports.

How do multiple financial accounts work?

If you have more than one financial account, the account with the Default badge is the account that automatically receives proceeds from your Stripe payments.

Additional business and checking accounts remain separate. They might support different currencies, funding methods, or money-management features, and they don’t automatically receive your payment proceeds.

Before adding, sending, or converting funds, confirm that you have selected the intended account.

FAQ

Do I need to do anything?

You don’t need to take action solely because your payments balance has become a default business account. You can continue accepting payments and using your available balance.

If Stripe needs information from you, you’ll see a notification or task in your Dashboard.

Is a default business account a bank account?

A default business account isn’t a bank account opened directly in your business’s name. It’s a financial account backed by a for-benefit-of arrangement with one of Stripe’s banking partners.

The banking partner holds funds for the benefit of Stripe customers, including your business. Stripe records your balance and displays your transactions and available money-management options in the Dashboard.

Review your account agreements and disclosures for the legal terms that apply to your account. Learn more about Stripe Treasury business accounts.

Are funds in my default business account FDIC insured?

No. Funds held in your default business account aren’t currently eligible for FDIC deposit insurance.

This applies to your default business account. Separate business and checking accounts have different terms and disclosures. Learn more about FDIC insurance eligibility

Where is my payments balance?

If your Dashboard shows a default business account, your existing pending and available payment funds are shown in that account instead of a separate payments balance.

Refunds, disputes, and payouts are also handled through your default business account. Payment processing and normal payment-availability timelines remain the same.

Do I need to transfer my earnings before I can use them?

No. Once your payment proceeds become available, you don’t need to transfer them to another business account or your external bank account before using a feature supported by your default business account.

Can payments settle into any of my business accounts?

No. Payment proceeds settle into the default business account. Additional business and checking accounts are separate and don’t automatically receive proceeds from your Stripe payments.

Why don’t I see a default business account?

Stripe is gradually rolling out default business accounts to eligible users in the United States, so this account setup isn’t available to everyone yet.

Stripe will inform you if it becomes available for your account. Until then, continue using your existing payments balance and the options shown in your Dashboard.

Do I need to update my payments integration?

No. You don’t need to update your existing payments integration because you received a default business account.

You can continue accepting and processing payments through your existing integration. The default business account changes where the resulting payment proceeds settle, not how your integration creates or processes payments.

Are there additional fees?

There’s no additional fee solely for having a default business account.

Fees might apply when you use certain money-management features, such as sending money or converting currencies. Review any fee shown in the Dashboard and the applicable pricing information before completing a transaction.

What is a settlement pause and what happens if my payment proceeds are placed in a settlement pause?

A settlement pause temporarily holds affected new or pending payment proceeds instead of adding them to your available balance. It doesn’t automatically affect funds that were already available, and you can continue accepting payments unless a separate restriction applies.

If Stripe needs information from you, you’ll see a task or notification in your Dashboard. Complete any requested steps and monitor your Dashboard and email for updates.

Learn more about settlement pauses.

Understanding your financial account

A financial account is a dedicated account connected to your Stripe account where you can hold funds. You can receive funds from external bank accounts and transfer money to your Stripe payments balance.

Your financial account is separate from your Stripe payments balance, which holds revenue from payments you process with Stripe. You can use a financial account to hold working capital on Stripe or set aside funds for specific business operations.

Types of financial accounts

Stripe offers two distinct types of financial accounts:

  • Business account: Holds and moves business funds. Available currencies vary by location and account configuration.
  • Checking account: Deposit account to hold business funds and support deposits and withdrawals. Available only to US businesses in US dollars (USD).

What can I do with a business account or checking account?

  • Hold funds in your local currency, separate from your payments revenue
  • Receive incoming transfers from external banks using local account details
  • Move money to your Stripe payments balance instantly, at no cost
  • Send funds to another business on Stripe instantly and for free

Where are financial accounts available?

Your financial account in each region has its own local account details. You can share these with any external bank to receive inbound transfers.

How is my money protected?

  • US: Funds are eligible for FDIC pass-through insurance up to 250,000 USD through Stripe’s partner banks.
  • UK: Funds are safeguarded in accordance with FCA requirements at authorized institutions.
  • EU: Funds are safeguarded under EU Payment Services Directive (PSD2) requirements.

Stripe Treasury is not itself a bank. Your funds are held at regulated financial institutions through Stripe’s banking partners.

FAQ

Do I need a separate financial account for each region?

Yes. Each region has its own financial account with its own currency and local account details. If you operate in multiple regions, you can hold USD, GBP, and EUR financial accounts simultaneously.

Is a business account a bank account?

No. A business account is not a bank account, but it offers similar functionality for holding and receiving funds. It’s issued through Stripe’s banking partners, and Stripe manages it on your behalf.

How do I access my financial account?

From the Stripe Dashboard, navigate to Balances and select your financial account to view your balance, transaction history, and account details.

Understanding your financial address

When you open a Stripe financial account, Stripe assigns it a financial address: a set of local bank account details that external banks and payment senders can use to send you money. In the US, this is a routing number and account number, in the UK, it’s a sort code and account number, and in the EU, it’s an IBAN and BIC.

To anyone sending you funds, your financial address looks and behaves exactly like a standard bank account. They enter the details into their bank, initiate a transfer, and the money arrives in your Stripe financial account.

Virtual bank accounts

A virtual bank account is a bank account that exists digitally rather than as an account held directly at a traditional bank. It has real, usable account details in the same format as any other account, but the account itself is managed by a financial technology provider (like Stripe) through partnerships with licensed banking institutions.

Your Stripe financial address is a virtual bank account. In practice this means:

  • It works like a real account. You can share the details with any bank or payment sender. Incoming transfers arrive just as they would to a conventional account.
  • It’s hosted by a regulated institution. The account details belong to Stripe’s banking partners - licensed banks who hold the underlying funds and are regulated in each region.
  • Stripe manages it on your behalf. You interact with your balance, transactions, and account settings through the Stripe Dashboard, not through a bank’s interface.

Virtual bank accounts are common in modern financial infrastructure. They’re how many payroll platforms, expense management tools, and embedded finance products give businesses local account details without requiring them to hold a direct relationship with a bank in every market.

One financial account, one financial address per currency

Each Stripe financial account has one financial address per currency. You can have multiple financial accounts per Stripe account.

These details are stable and don’t change unless Stripe explicitly reissues them. You can share them freely with banks, counterparties, or internal finance systems as a standing destination for incoming funds.

FAQ

Is my financial address the same as a bank account number?

Functionally, yes. It works the same way from a sender’s perspective. The underlying infrastructure is a virtual account hosted through Stripe’s banking partners rather than a direct account at a high-street bank.

Can I use my financial address to receive payments from anyone?

Yes. Anyone with a bank account in the same payment network can send funds to your financial address. There’s no restriction on who can send - it works like any standard bank account destination.

Will my financial address ever change?

In normal circumstances, no. Your financial address is stable and can be treated as a permanent account destination. Stripe will notify you if a change is ever required.

Can I have multiple financial addresses for the same currency?

Each financial account has one financial address. If your use case requires multiple receiving accounts (for example, to segregate funds by business unit), contact Stripe to discuss your options.

US payment methods for funding your financial accounts

Your US financial accounts can receive funds over three payment networks: ACH, RTP, and Fedwire. All use the same account details: the routing number and account number found in the Stripe Dashboard under Financial account > Account details.

ACH

Automated Clearing House (ACH) is the network behind direct deposits, bill payments, and the majority of business-to-business fund movements. Virtually every US bank account can send and receive ACH.

ACH processes in batches throughout the business day rather than individually, which is why transfers can take up to three business days to settle. It operates on US business days only. There are no fees for ACH transfers.

There are two ways to move money via ACH:

  • ACH Credit (push): You instruct your bank to push funds to your Stripe financial account. You control the timing and amount entirely. Depending on your bank, you may be able to send these as Same Day ACH for faster settlement.
  • ACH Debit (pull): You authorize Stripe to pull funds from your external bank account. Useful for recurring or scheduled top-ups without involving your bank each time.

Best for: Regular, predictable top-ups where a 0-3 day window is acceptable.

Fedwire

Fedwire is the Federal Reserve’s settlement system for same-day, high-value wire transfers. Unlike ACH’s batch processing, each Fedwire payment settles individually and immediately - funds arrive at Stripe within minutes of your bank submitting the transfer.

Fedwire operates on US business days during Federal Reserve hours. To receive same-day credit, your bank must submit the wire before 5pm ET - and your bank’s own internal cutoff is typically earlier, often 4-4:30pm ET. There is no upper limit on Fedwire transfer amounts.

Best for: Large or time-sensitive transfers where same-day settlement is required.

RTP

Real-Time Payments (RTP) lets you send funds from an external bank to your Stripe financial account in real time. Unlike ACH, RTP payments are processed individually rather than in batches, so funds are typically available within minutes.

RTP is available 24/7, including weekends and holidays, with no cutoff time. To send an RTP payment, give your bank the routing number and account number for your Stripe financial account. RTP is a push payment, meaning you instruct your external bank to send the funds.

RTP payments are final and can’t be reversed. Your external bank must support RTP to send one. There are no fees for incoming RTP payments.

Best for: Time-sensitive transfers when you need funds quickly outside standard business hours.

Verification of Payee support for Treasury

Verification of Payee (VoP) regulation launched in October 2025 and helps prevent fraud and misdirected payments on the SEPA payment system. When you initiate a payout to a European recipient or fund an EU business account, VoP requires that you check whether the beneficiary name matches the name registered with the receiving account. This verification happens in real-time before the payment is processed, helping ensure payments reach their intended recipient.

Topping up your business account

You can top up your business account by sending a SEPA bank transfer to your Financial Address. To ensure VoP returns a match, you should use the exact business name as it appears in your Stripe account.

Where to find your account holder name:

  • Navigate to your business account
  • Click “Move Money” and then “Add money for payouts”
  • Select the “EUR business account” and click External bank transfer in the side modal
  • Look for “account holder name”; this is the exact name that should be used for incoming bank transfers

Sending payouts

When initiating a payout to an EU recipient in the Dashboard, Stripe will perform the VoP check. In case of a mismatch or close match, you will be prompted to acknowledge the difference and either edit the details or cancel the payout.

To ensure successful payouts from the first try, always collect the exact account holder details from your recipients, or ask them to provide the information themselves via Hosted Recipient Onboarding.

Treasury for platforms

Can I create more than one financial account for a connected account?

By default, platforms onboarded to Treasury for platforms can create up to three financial accounts per connected account. Platforms can contact our dedicated support teams if additional financial accounts are required.

Can we generate statements for financial accounts?

We don’t provide statements for financial accounts, but you’re welcome to create customized financial account statements on your end and issue those on a regular cadence for your users. If you choose to create customized statements there are a number of compliance requirements you need to follow, which you can read more about in our Treasury for platforms product documentation.

How do I know if my account is eligible for Treasury for platforms?

There are some limitations to keep in mind as you evaluate whether a Stripe Treasury for platforms integration is a good fit for your business:

  • Geography: Treasury for platforms is available in the United States, UK (public preview) and EU (private preview) for both platform and connected accounts.
  • Connected accounts: Treasury for platforms only supports connected accounts with the following characteristics, also known as ‘Custom’:
    • Platform owns onboarding and loss liability
    • Connected account dashboards are not made available by Stripe
  • Users: Treasury for platforms is only available for businesses located in the United States, UK and EU.
  • Restricted business types: Review Stripe’s Restricted Businesses List as well as Treasury for platforms requirements for an overview of what kinds of businesses are supportable on Treasury.
  • Usage: Financial accounts must be used for business purposes only — they can’t be used for consumer purposes.

Physical presence requirement FAQ

  • What’s changing?
  • Why is Stripe making these changes?
  • How will screening impact Issuing, Treasury, and Opal users?
  • Will this requirement impact access to other Stripe products?
  • How will this change impact Stripe Atlas users?
  • What are physical mailbox and virtual address services?
  • What is a registered agent?
  • Which account types will be screened?
  • Which address types will be screened?
  • How will Stripe determine if an address is from a registered agent, mailbox service or virtual address service?
  • What happens when an address is flagged?

What’s changing?

Starting July 1, 2025, Stripe requires that Issuing, Treasury, and Opal US-based accounts have a physical presence in the United States. Stripe will automatically screen Issuing, Treasury, and Opal US-based accounts to ensure they have a physical presence in the United States.

We no longer allow addresses associated with mailbox services and virtual address services as a physical presence.

Why is Stripe making these changes?

The partners we use to provide financial products in the United States require the businesses we support to have a physical presence—not just a mailing address—in the United States.

How will screening impact Issuing, Treasury, and Opal users?

For existing accounts, we’ll complete a one-time screening of all accounts with Issuing, Treasury, or Opal capabilities on July 1, 2025.

For new accounts, we’ll complete screening whenever you request Issuing or Treasury capabilities for a connected account.

We’ll automatically screen addresses whenever you:

  • Request Issuing or Treasury capabilities for a connected account
  • Update an address for an account with Issuing, Treasury, or Opal capabilities

If we identify an address we can’t support, your attempt to add these capabilities will fail and we will share more details via email and the accounts.updated webhook.

Will this requirement impact access to other Stripe products?

The physical presence requirement will only apply to US accounts with Issuing, Treasury, or Opal capabilities. While US accounts with business or account representative addresses associated with registered agents, mailbox services, or virtual address services will no longer be able to access those capabilities, those accounts will still be able to use Stripe for payment processing and other products.

How will this change impact Stripe Atlas users?

Because Delaware requires all companies formed in the state to have a registered agent for the specific purpose of receiving mail correspondence from the state, Stripe Atlas provides registered agent services for all companies formed on Atlas. This registered agent address doesn’t serve as the company’s operating address or physical address.

All users enabling Issuing, Treasury, or Opal must provide evidence of a physical US address. For Atlas companies, this may be a personal address or the address where your company physically does business, but it can’t be your Atlas registered agent, nor can it be a mailbox or virtual address service.

For more information, see Atlas-provided registered agents and Managing your registered agent subscription.

What are physical mailbox and virtual address services?

Mailbox services and virtual address services provide individuals or businesses with a real street address to receive mail and packages. Physical mailbox services offer in-person pickup, while virtual address services digitize incoming mail for online viewing, forwarding, or management. Addresses associated with physical mailbox services and virtual address services do not meet our requirements for US platforms using Issuing or Treasury, or US connected accounts with Issuing or Treasury capabilities.

What is a registered agent?

A registered agent is a person or company authorized to receive official legal documents and government notices on behalf of a business, such as service of process. Addresses associated with registered agents don’t meet our requirements for US platforms using Issuing or Treasury, or US connected accounts with Issuing or Treasury capabilities.

Which account types will be screened?

The screening will apply to both US platforms using Issuing or Treasury and US connected accounts with Issuing or Treasury capabilities.

Which address types will be screened?

The screening will apply to the business address and account representative address associated with US Issuing, Treasury, and Opal accounts. These address types are used to assess eligibility for financial products.

Other individuals, such as beneficial owners who aren’t account representatives, will still be able to use an address associated with a registered agent, mailbox service, or virtual address service.

How will Stripe determine if an address is from a registered agent, mailbox service, or virtual address service?

Stripe will screen business and account representative addresses against a proprietary list of addresses associated with registered agents, mailbox services and virtual address services. If an address you provided matches one on this list, we will notify you immediately via email and webhook with details about next steps.

What happens when an address is flagged?

If an address is flagged, we will notify you immediately. You will be prompted to update the address to one that is not associated with a registered agent, mailbox service or virtual address service. If you believe an address was flagged in error, you will be able submit an appeal with supporting documents.

  • For new users: your attempt to add Issuing or Treasury capabilities will fail and we will notify you immediately of the reason using the accounts.updated webhook.
  • For existing users: if the flagged address is not updated or successfully appealed within 30 days, the account will no longer be able to access Issuing, Treasury, or Opal capabilities.
