Enhanced identity verification for Singapore-based accounts

Some Singapore-based Stripe accounts are required to complete enhanced identity verification. This means sharing your personal identity information using Singpass, the Singapore government’s digital identity platform.

What is Singpass?

Singpass is an electronic identity verification platform operated by the Singapore government, and is available to most Singapore residents. You can learn more about Singpass eligibility.

How do I use Singpass with Stripe?

When you activate your Stripe account, you’ll be prompted to use Singpass to verify your identity if you are eligible. You’ll need a Singpass account before you can begin the process, so you’ll be prompted to create one if you don’t already have one.You can learn more about creating a Singpass account.

Can I choose to not use Singpass with Stripe?

You can choose not to use Singpass and instead verify your details directly with Stripe.

If you don’t use Singpass to verify your identity, you may have to upload additional documentation, such as a scan of your identity document.

What data will Stripe obtain through Singpass?

We will obtain the following personal identifiable information:

  • Name (including any aliases)
  • Date of birth
  • NRIC/FIN number
  • Registered address
  • Email address
  • Phone number

Stripe is obligated to collect these fields to meet our KYC (know your customer) responsibilities as a financial services provider.

Europe - Updated verification requirements for connected accounts of Platforms

Last updated: August 2026

Stripe regularly reviews and updates verification requirements to provide best-in-class protections for its users. These changes vary by region, guided by different regulatory, network, and partner rules, which inform the information we collect and verify to understand who our customers are.

For connected accounts in Europe, we are updating Know Your Customer (KYC) requirements, which include identity verification, legal entity verification and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) and director verification. These updates apply to all regulated financial services across 33 countries in Europe.

If you are a platform that is responsible for collecting requirement information from your connected accounts, you will need to update your integration to handle these changes. This will ensure your connected accounts meet the new requirements, allowing them to continue accepting card payments and receiving payouts without interruption.

Visit your Dashboard to learn more and begin preparing for these changes.

FAQ

  • Why is Stripe updating verification requirements for these accounts?
  • What’s changing for connected accounts in Europe?
  • Which capabilities will be impacted by these new requirements?
  • What changes do Platforms need to implement?
  • What is the timeline for my existing connected accounts to provide information?
  • Which individuals associated with the account will need to undergo verifications?
  • What about my connected accounts for which Stripe handles onboarding?
  • Where can I track the progress of my connected accounts through the Europe verification update?

Why is Stripe updating verification requirements for these accounts?

Stripe regularly reviews and updates its verification requirements to stay current with financial regulations and ensure businesses that use Stripe are compliant. For businesses based in Europe that process payments with us or use our products and services, we’re updating how we collect, validate, and verify business and personal information in line with local regulations including the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and Central Bank of Ireland (CBI)

What’s changing for connected accounts in Europe?

In order to meet higher KYC standards, some connected accounts in Europe will need to complete:

  • Enhanced identity verification. Some individuals associated with connected accounts may need to provide additional information to verify their identity. Stripe will attempt to programmatically verify the information provided upon onboarding. If this fails, connected accounts can choose to:
    • Complete selfie verification via Stripe Identity
    • Provide updated information to Stripe, including a new optional National ID number
    • Upload 2 separate documents:
      • One as Proof of Identity such as a passport or a driver’s license
      • One as Proof of Home Address such as a utility bill or a bank statement
  • Legal entity verification. Some accounts will need to provide additional information to verify the company name, address, and registration number. If we are unable to verify your business programmatically, Stripe may request additional Proof of Business documentation in order to verify legal entities.
  • Ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) and director verification. Some connected accounts will need to provide additional information in order for Stripe to verify the relationship between the business and its UBO(s) and/or director(s).

UBO and director verifications in Europe are based on European regulatory requirements which require:

  • Verification of ultimate beneficial owner(s) and/or director(s) relationship to the legal entity (LE); and
  • Occasionally, identity verification of the ultimate beneficial owner, when additional information is required

Read more about beneficial ownership.

View Acceptable verification documents by country.

Which capabilities will be impacted by these new requirements?

These updates apply to your accounts that have card_payments capability enabled across 33 countries in Europe.

What changes do Platforms need to implement?

Custom Connect platforms must:

Update their integration:

  • By April 1, 2026: Platforms with only individual connected account types must update their onboarding flows. New connected accounts in Europe created after this date must meet the updated requirements.
  • By May 1, 2026: Platforms with any company or other legal entity connected accounts types have until May 1st to update their onboarding flows. New connected accounts in Europe created after this date must meet the updated requirements.

Collect updated business information for existing users by October 31, 2026. Existing connected accounts must meet the updated requirements to continue to receive payouts. They may also experience further capability restrictions.

Standard/Express/UA1&UA2 platforms do not require any integration changes. Stripe will reach out to their connected accounts directly to collect updated business information.

Find more details on how to prepare in your Dashboard.

What changes do Custom Platforms have to make to their integration?

If you use an API-based flow to onboard your connected accounts, you must update your integration to handle all requirement changes. Platforms have three options to choose from when deciding how to adjust their onboarding flow to ensure connected accounts meet these requirements.

Even if a custom platform has an API integration, they can still take advantage of hosted or embedded onboarding to implement the updated onboarding requirements.

  • Embedded Onboarding:** Add customizable embedded onboarding components to your site. These dynamically update to reflect new requirements.
  • Stripe Hosted: Send users to our hosted onboarding experience. This flow also updates automatically to reflect new requirements, but provides less customization. When your new connected accounts provide business information we’re unable to verify, we’ll surface detailed verification responses via the Accounts API. You’ll need to adjust your integration to handle new verification responses.
  • API Onboarding: Modify your existing onboarding flow using detailed verification responses from the Accounts API. This allows the most control, but requires the most effort to maintain.

Visit our Integration guide to learn about the changes, review timelines and access technical resources for updating your integration. We’ve released API updates to support new verification workflows for accounts in Europe, allowing you to prepare for the necessary changes to your integration.

What is the timeline for my existing connected accounts to provide information?

Europe-based connected accounts are subject to new requirements with the following key deadlines:

  • Starting March 2026: You’ll be able to see an estimate of impacted accounts via Dashboard and API.
  • April 1, 2026: New accounts for platforms that only have individual connected accounts must meet the updated requirements before they can be successfully onboarded.
  • May 1, 2026: New accounts for platforms that only have company connected accounts, or a mix of company and individual connected accounts, must meet the updated requirements before they can be successfully onboarded.
  • June 2026: New requirements are due for existing accounts.
  • June 2026 - October 31, 2026: To avoid restrictions, the updated requirements for each account must be verified by that account’s due date.

Which individuals associated with the account will need to undergo verifications?

Account Representatives , Ultimate Beneficiary Owners and Directors will need to undergo enhanced identity verification. Stripe will attempt to programmatically verify the information that was provided during onboarding. If this fails, individuals on connected accounts can choose to:

  • Complete selfie verification via Stripe Identity
  • Provide updated information to Stripe, including a new optional National ID number
  • Upload 2 separate documents:
    • One as Proof of Identity such as a passport or a driving licence
    • One as Proof of Home Address such as a utility bill or a bank statement

View the list of acceptable documents for each country.

What about my connected accounts for which Stripe handles onboarding?

If you have connected accounts in Europe where Stripe manages onboarding, including Standard and Express connected accounts, refer to the support article.

Where can I track the progress of my connected accounts through the Europe verification update?

You can track the progress of your connected accounts through both the Dashboard and API.

In your Dashboard, go to Connect > Compliance. Under Europe Requirement Update, you’ll see a summary of all your connected accounts in scope for the Europe verification update, broken down by status. This includes accounts that have already met the updated requirements, accounts that still have outstanding verifications, and accounts that haven’t started yet.

To move accounts through the update, review your connected accounts list and prioritize those with a Restricted or Restricted soon status. Select an account to see which requirements are outstanding and what information that account must provide.

To avoid restrictions, the updated requirements for each account must be verified by that account’s due date. Find more details on how to review compliance information in your Dashboard.

Can’t find what you’re looking for? See our FAQ for Platforms.

Europe verification updates for connected accounts where Stripe is responsible for collecting required information

Last updated: March 2026

This article is for platforms where Stripe is responsible for collecting required information from your connected accounts, including Standard and Express.

Overview

Stripe regularly reviews and updates verification requirements to provide best-in-class protections for its users. These changes vary by region, guided by different regulatory, network, and partner rules, which inform the information we collect and verify to understand who our customers are.

For connected accounts in Europe, we are updating Know Your Customer (KYC) requirements, which include identity verification, legal entity verification and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) and director verification. These updates apply to your accounts that have card_payments capability enabled across 33 countries in Europe.

Stripe helps your connected accounts remain compliant as verification requirements evolve. As a platform with accounts where Stripe is responsible for collecting required information, your new and existing users will see updated verification requirements.

What does this mean for your new connected accounts?

Starting November 2025, new identity verification requirements for new connected accounts will take effect. These requirements will be gradually introduced for your new connected accounts. The Stripe-hosted onboarding or embedded onboarding flows will automatically update to reflect new verification requirements.

Additional requirements for ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) and director verification will be rolled out in January 2026.

What does this mean for your existing connected accounts?

Starting January 2026, we will begin outreach to existing connected accounts to collect updated or additional information, continuing throughout the year. These accounts will have ample time to complete verification requirements before any impact on their capabilities.

What’s changing for connected accounts in Europe?

In order to meet higher KYC standards, some connected accounts in Europe will need to complete:

  • Enhanced identity verification. Some individuals associated with connected accounts may need to provide additional information to verify their identity. Stripe will attempt to programmatically verify the information provided upon onboarding. If this fails, connected accounts can choose to:
    • Complete selfie verification via Stripe Identity
    • Provide updated information to Stripe, including a new optional National ID number
    • Upload 2 separate documents:
      • One as Proof of Identity such as a passport or a driver’s license
      • One as Proof of Home Address such as a utility bill or a bank statement
  • Legal entity verification. Some accounts will need to provide additional information to verify the company name, address, and registration number. If we are unable to verify your business programmatically, Stripe may request additional Proof of Business documentation in order to verify legal entities.
  • Ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) and director verification. Some connected accounts will need to provide additional information in order for Stripe to verify the relationship between the business and its UBO(s) and/or director(s).

UBO and director verifications in Europe are based on European regulatory requirements which require:

  • Verification of ultimate beneficial owner(s) and/or director(s) relationship to the legal entity (LE); and
  • Occasionally, identity verification of the ultimate beneficial owner, when additional information is required

Read more about beneficial ownership.

View Acceptable verification documents by country.

How should I prepare for this change?

We recommend you get familiar with what’s changing and to review the updated requirements your new and existing connected accounts will encounter.

Stripe-hosted onboarding or embedded onboarding flows, will automatically update to reflect these changes.

Is Stripe responsible for collecting information from my connected accounts?

If you have connected accounts in Europe where Stripe manages onboarding, we’ll notify you when these updates to verification requirements impact your users.

If you utilize Stripe-hosted or embedded onboarding flows these flows will automatically update to reflect the latest requirements, and we’ll reach out directly to your connected accounts through hosted flows or embedded components to collect the updated information.

What happens if my new connected accounts don’t provide the required information during onboarding?

If an account doesn’t provide the required information during onboarding or by the due date listed in the user’s dashboard, their ability to accept payments and receive payouts will be paused. After an account has been paused and provides the required information, the account regains their ability to receive payouts and accept charges.

How can I monitor remediation success or help my connected accounts action these tasks?

Once Stripe begins outreach to your existing connected accounts, you will be able to monitor remediation success in your Stripe Dashboard and via API.

Why is Stripe updating verification requirements for these accounts?

Stripe regularly reviews and updates its verification requirements to stay current with financial regulations, reduce fraud and ensure businesses that use Stripe are compliant. For businesses based in Europe that process payments with us or use our products and services, we’re updating how we collect, validate, and verify business and personal information in line with local regulations including the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and Central Bank of Ireland (CBI)

Europe: Ultimate beneficial owner and Director definitions

Some accounts in Europe will need to provide additional information in order for Stripe to verify the relationship between the business and its ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) or Directors.

UBO and Director verifications in Europe are based on European regulatory requirements which require:

  • Relation verification of UBOs or Directors relationship to the legal entity (LE)
  • In certain cases, verifying the identity of the UBOs or Directors to meet regulatory standards and safeguard your account.

Definitions

Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs): The individual(s) who own or control, directly or indirectly, more than 25% of a legal entity, including companies, corporations, LLCs and partnerships.

Directors: Members of the board of directors of the business, and/or any other senior person responsible for managing the business. Examples include CEO, COO, President, Managing Director, and Executive Director.

Verification of UBOs or Directors relationship

Stripe will first attempt to programmatically verify a person’s relationship to the legal entity by automatically cross-referencing public and government data sources.

If this programmatic verification isn’t successful, you may need to upload an official document or sign a digital attestation.

Identity verification of UBOs or Directors

Stripe needs to verify UBOs or Directors added to your account. We’ll attempt to verify their identity using the information provided on the account. If this fails, individuals may need to:

  • Complete selfie verification via Stripe Identity.
  • Provide updated information to Stripe, including a new optional National ID number.
  • Upload 2 separate documents:
    • Proof of Identity, such as a passport or a driving licence
    • Proof of Home Address, such as a utility bill or a bank statement

View the list of acceptable documents for each country.

What should I do if my business is owned fully or partially by a holding company?

As part of our regulatory requirements, Stripe is obligated to verify the identity of any individual who holds more than 25% ownership in the business entity linked to your Stripe account.

This requirement extends to both direct and indirect ownership. For instance, if your business is partially owned by a holding company, trust, or another legal entity, we are required to identify the individuals who own or control those entities, provided their stake amounts to more than 25% of the company connected to your Stripe account.

Read more about calculating beneficial ownership percentages.

Exceptions to the list of Accepted Documents for non-US merchants

If you are not able to verify your documents programmatically, Stripe might need to request additional documentation in order to verify the individuals as well as the businesses connected to a Stripe account.

Please provide Stripe with the additional documents if you are eligible for one of the exceptions listed below.

Proof of address document is issued in your partner’s name

You must supply:

  • Proof of address documentation in your partner’s name
  • Marriage or civil partnership certificate with both your name (as displayed on your Stripe account) and your partner’s name (as displayed on the proof of address documentation)

These documents will need to be merged and uploaded as one file. The file should be uploaded in .pdf format with a size of less than 10Mb.

Proof of address document is issued in your parent/guardian’s name

You must supply:

  • Proof of address documentation in your parent/guardian’s name
  • Birth/legal guardianship certificate with both your name (as displayed on your Stripe account) and your parent/legal guardian’s name (as displayed on the proof of address documentation)

These documents will need to be merged and uploaded as one file. The file should be uploaded in .pdf format with a size of less than 10Mb.

Proof of address document was issued prior to finalizing legal name change

You must supply:

  • Proof of address documentation in your previous name prior to the legal name change
  • Official name change certification clearly showing your your new name (as displayed on your Stripe account) and your previous name (as displayed on the proof of address documentation)

These documents will need to be merged and uploaded as one file. The file should be uploaded in .pdf format with a size of less than 10Mb.

Irish-registered businesses: How to collect Beneficial Ownership Information

Log into your business RBO account, take a screenshot of the data, and upload it via the Dashboard. Click Proof of Business Registration and then Screenshot from online registration.

All businesses with legal entities incorporated in Ireland are required to file data with the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership of Companies and Industrial and Provident Societies (RBO). This is in addition to the requirement to file company details with the Companies Registration Office (CRO) in Ireland.

See Company beneficial ownership and director requirement for general background.

Not required to file

You are NOT required to file data with the RBO if you are:

  • An unincorporated business e.g. Sole Trader / Unincorporated Partnership
  • An unincorporated business that has a registered business name with the CRO
  • A company listed on a regulated market e.g. Public Limited Company (Plc)
  • A branch of an entity that is not incorporated in Ireland
  • Charities / Non-profit organization (NPOs) with no incorporated legal entity

Ensure your Type of business selection on the Tax details Settings page of the Dashboard correctly reflects your status.

Provided your business is in scope based on your Type of business selection, Stripe will check the business name, business number, and beneficial ownership information you have submitted on your account against the information listed on the RBO. This includes your:

  • Company Registration Number (CRN)
  • Company Name
  • Company status
  • The number of Beneficial Owners
  • The name, date of birth, and % of ownership if applicable for each beneficial owner

No action is needed if your business name, business number, and beneficial ownership information match the information submitted to Stripe.

If your information doesn’t match

If your beneficial ownership information submitted with Stripe does not completely match the information listed on the RBO (for example your beneficial owners names do not match the data listed on the RBO), then there is a discrepancy that Stripe is required by law to report to the RBO.

This doesn’t affect your ability to accept payments or make payouts to your bank account. Review the information listed on the RBO and the information you submitted on Stripe at any time and make necessary updates.

If your company number submitted on Stripe cannot be found in the RBO database (our search returns a ‘Not found’ result), or if your business name submitted on Stripe does not completely match the name listed on the RBO, or if your Business status is inactive on the RBO, Stripe will ask you to upload documentation about your account on the RBO website.

Before uploading any document, ensure your company number, business name and beneficial owner information currently saved on Stripe in the Dashboard matches the information on the RBO.

The most common reasons we are unable to find registered businesses in the RBO are:

  • The number for your business or company name on the RBO and Stripe don’t match. Update it in the Dashboard.
  • Your Type of business on Stripe is not accurate. Update it in the Dashboard so Stripe knows you aren’t required to file data with the RBO.
  • Verify if your company status is active on the RBO. If not, contact the RBO to resolve the issue.
  • You’re a newly established business and your company’s incorporation and/or beneficial ownership details have yet to be filed. If so, complete your beneficial ownership registration with the RBO and submit proof to Stripe, via the Dashboard.

If you can’t provide proof that your company has in fact registered with the RBO, then your ability to accept payments and get payouts to your bank account will be paused. We are also required to notify the Registrar that your legal entity does not match the information in the RBO.

Legal entity documentation requirement

Stripe is required to collect, verify, and maintain information on the legal entity—business or nonprofit—associated with each Stripe account. These requirements come from our regulators and financial partners and are intended to prevent bad actors from using legal entities to hide terrorist financing, money laundering, tax evasion, and other financial crimes.

One of the primary reasons we can get users up and running so quickly is our rather unique registration process. When signing up for a Stripe account, we use the information you enter to programmatically verify your legal entity and the individuals associated with it. To complete the verification process, we may need to reach out for a copy of your business formation or non-profit registration documents.

Accepted documentation

The exact documents vary by country and legal entity type, but Stripe can typically accept a copy of your:

  • partnership agreement,
  • company constitution/articles of association,
  • certificate of incorporation, or
  • certificate of nonprofit registration

What if I don’t have any of these documents?

The list of acceptable documents varies by country and entity type. If you are setting up an account for an entity that does not have any of the above documents, contact us.

Phone number requirements for US Stripe accounts

Phone numbers are required as part of Stripe’s onboarding process. Stripe is required by our financial partners to collect phone numbers associated with the business/legal entity and/or the persons associated with the Stripe account. This information helps Stripe further understand the business and the persons associated with the account.

When opening a Stripe account in the United States, we require:

  • Business phone number: A valid and active US-based phone number.
    • If your Stripe account is set up as Individual/Sole Prop type, a business phone number isn’t required.
    • If your Stripe account incorporated a company via Stripe Atlas, the business phone number can be in any country.
  • Customer support number: A valid phone number (can be in any country). This can be the same as the business phone number.
    • The customer support number is shared with card networks and surfaced on cardmember statements and transaction details including payment statements, invoices, and receipts.
  • Representative/owner number: A valid phone number (can be in any country).
    • If your Stripe account is set up as Individual/Sole Prop type, the representative/owner phone number must be an active US-based phone number.

Additional Information

  • Our Privacy Policy explains how and for what purposes we collect, use, retain, disclose, and safeguard any personal data you provide to us.

Representative Authority Verification

In certain markets, such as Singapore, we are required to verify that the business representative holds a position of authority in the business. A position of authority is defined differently for companies, non-profits, and government agencies:

Company

The business’ representative must be listed on ACRA Bizfile as a key officer, which could be any of the following roles: Owner, Director, Managing Director, CEO, Partner, General Partner, or Trustee.

If the key officers listed on ACRA are unable to manage the Stripe account, a Letter of Authorization (Template) signed by a key officer will be required (letter should be dated within the last 12 months and names should be in English). This letter must authorize a designated person to be listed as the representative of their company. This designated person can then be verified as a representative on Stripe.

Non-profit:

The business’ representative must be listed on charities.gov.sg as an office bearer, which could be any of the following roles: President, Vice President, Deputy President, Director, Deputy Director, CEO, Treasurer, Secretary, Chairman, Vice Chairman, or Trustee.

If the office bearers listed on charities.gov.sg are unable to manage the Stripe account, a Letter of Authorization (Template) signed by a key officer authorizing a designated person as a representative of their company will be required (letter should be dated within the last 12 months). This person can then be verified as a representative on Stripe.

Information required from the Account Representative

The representative must provide the following information:

  • Proof of ID
  • Proof of Address
  • Proof of liveness

These requirements can all be fulfilled directly through the Singpass option available on the dashboard. If Singpass is not used or if Stripe is unable to obtain any necessary information from Singpass, alternative documentation will be requested from the user.

Resolving SSN/ITIN errors

What should I do if I don’t have a US SSN?

Accounts set up as Individual or Sole props, which had previously registered with a non-US representative, will need to provide updated business representative information, including a US TIN. If you do not have a US SSN, you can consider changing your business type to correctly reflect your current company structure.

For business owners who have registered their company with a government body, the appropriate business type on Stripe will now likely be ‘Company,’ with the specific business structure reflecting the method of incorporation. In contrast, unregistered entities will likely have to select ’Individual’ for their business type.

To modify your business type to match these new guidelines, please visit this link and follow the steps:

  • Log into the Stripe Dashboard
  • Once in the Stripe Dashboard, navigate to Settings (gearbox in the top right of the Dashboard), and click on Settings
  • Scroll down to the “Business Settings” section and select “Tax details”
  • Change your business type to reflect your business

What should I do if my SSN/ITIN verification is failing?

If you have updated your 9 digit US SSN/ITIN and the verification has failed, please check the full name of the account representative we have on file. Stripe uses your legal name and associated SSN/ITIN to verify your identity.

What should I do if I need to change my business representative?

If the business representative information we have on file is outdated, please follow the steps laid out on this page.

What should I do if I need to change my business type?

To modify your business type, please visit this link and follow the steps:

  • Log into the Stripe Dashboard
  • Once in the Stripe Dashboard, navigate to Settings (gearbox in the top right of the Dashboard), and click on Settings
  • Scroll down to the “Business Settings” section and select “Tax details”
  • Change your business type to reflect your business

Singapore verification requirements for platforms: Updates and FAQ

The Dashboard’s Accounts to review page shows the status of connected accounts impacted by any changes to verification requirements. To filter by country, click More filters > Verification requirement and then check the box for the country you want to see. Here’s a pre-filtered link for Singapore.

To make sure you’re up to date with the latest changes, we also recommend reviewing the new verification errors. And, you can listen for risk-related account updates via the Accounts API.

Deadlines

Custom:

  • New Custom connected accounts created on or after April 29, 2025: Must meet the updated requirements during onboarding. Otherwise, they won’t be able to accept payments.
  • Existing Custom connected accounts: All future_requirements will become current requirements on May 20th, 2025. If they haven’t provided the required information, they won’t be able to receive payouts beginning June 24, 2025, and won’t be able to accept payments beginning July 15, 2025.

All other connected accounts:

  • New connected accounts created on or after April 8, 2025: Must meet the updated requirements otherwise, they won’t be able to accept payments.
  • Existing connected accounts will start receiving requirements on a rolling schedule starting April 1, 2025.

FAQ

What accounts are affected?

The updated verification requirements apply to all connected accounts with the card_payments or transfers capability enabled in Singapore.

How can I see which of my accounts require updated information?

See the status of affected connected accounts in the new Accounts to review list in the Dashboard. To filter by country, click More filters > Verification requirement and then check the box for the country you want to see.

What information is required to onboard new connected accounts in Singapore?

Use the interactive form to see details of the required verification info for specific account configurations.

How do my existing accounts provide the new information required?

For connected accounts that have access to the Stripe Dashboard, to the Express Dashboard, or to the embedded notification banner, Stripe will contact the account directly with details about the business information they need to provide and the deadline to respond.

For connected accounts with platform-owned verification, you will need to take action to help your connected accounts provide this information or provide it yourself. See the Singapore Connected Account with platform-owned verification FAQ for more details.

information or provide it yourself. See Canada Connected Accounts with platform-owned verification FAQ for more details.

What new information do they need to provide?
  • Business types and structures supported. We’re collecting company.structure to accurately model legal structures.
  • Business and personal information collected. We’re updating the information collection and verification requirements for all businesses currently supported today.
  • How business and personal information is verified. We’re updating our criteria for valid business and personal information, and introducing new error codes when we’re unable to accept or verify the information provided.
What happens if my connected accounts don’t provide the required information?

If an account doesn’t provide the required information by the listed due date, their ability to accept payments and receive payouts will be paused:

  • For Platform-loss liable connected accounts: Typically, they will no longer be able to make payouts 14 days after the due date has passed, and they will no longer be able to accept payments 28 days after the due date has passed.
  • For all other types of connected accounts: Typically, they will no longer be able to make payouts immediately after the due date has passed, and they will no longer be able to accept payments 21 days after the due date has passed.

However, these timelines may vary for certain types of issues.

Why is Stripe updating verification requirements for these accounts?

Payments regulations aim to create a safer, more secure financial ecosystem by helping prevent crimes like money laundering, fraud, and tax evasion. Stripe has certain Know Your Customer (KYC) obligations that require us to collect, verify, and maintain identity information about our users, and for any individuals who ultimately own, control, or direct them. These requirements are frequently updated by Stripe, financial service regulators, card networks, and other financial institutions.

Will requirements continue to change?

Yes. As regulatory requirements evolve globally, we expect our onboarding requirements to continue changing as well. If you use embedded onboarding components or Stripe-hosted onboarding, we’ll automatically update your onboarding flow to handle the latest verification requirements. If you use API-based onboarding, you’ll need to manually modify your onboarding flow whenever requirements change. Learn more about the different onboarding methods in our documentation.

Stripe Verification Guide

Stripe is required to verify the businesses and people using its services. This guide covers tips for completing your account verification, and what to do if you encounter any errors.

Start your verification in the Stripe Dashboard. This guide covers common troubleshooting steps. The requirements displayed in your Stripe Dashboard and the country-specific acceptable document list take precedence.

Verification tips

  • Ensure your business information matches. Enter your details - business name, tax or registration ID and address - exactly as they appear on official records. Any documents you submit must show matching information.
  • Provide complete information for your authorized representative and any owners, directors, or executives Stripe asks you to identify.
  • Respond to any additional requirements promptly. You’ll find any requests for additional information under account status. If Stripe requests documents, use the checklist below to help ensure your document is accepted.

Troubleshooting verification errors

You may run into issues while completing your verification on Stripe. Follow the steps below to understand how to address common verification errors faced by new Stripe users.

If you’re a Connect Platform, the following guidance also applies to your Standard/Express Connected Accounts completing their account verification via the Stripe Dashboard.

Step 1: Navigate to the Stripe Dashboard

Open the verification requirement in your Stripe Dashboard. Confirm what Stripe is asking you to verify and the exact error displayed.

For Connect Platforms troubleshooting on behalf of your Connected Accounts, navigate to each Connected Account’s individual profile page to locate its verification error reason(s).

Step 2: Identify your verification error and next steps

Most verification errors occur due to a mismatch of information between your Stripe account and the uploaded document, or an incorrect document type. Learn how to fix common error types below.

Error Type

Checks to Do

Next Steps

Name mismatch (Individual)

  • Full legal name on the uploaded document exactly matches the legal name of the Account Representative, Director or Owner in your Stripe account settings.

  • Common issues: missing middle or additional names, suffixes, spacing, name order, and former names.

  • Correct any mismatches in the full legal name for the relevant individual on your Stripe Dashboard.

  • If the name has changed but the individual doesn’t have an ID with the new name yet, contact Stripe Support and provide paperwork (for example, a marriage certificate dated within the past twelve months) confirming the name change.

Business name mismatch or missing

  • For US users: Ensure the legal name entered on your Stripe account matches the TIN in the IRS database, or the legal business name on your uploaded document.

  • For non-US users: Legal entity name on the uploaded document exactly matches the legal business name on your Stripe account settings.

  • Common mismatches: Using the “Doing Business As” (DBA) name or trading name on the Stripe dashboard, instead of the legal business name.

  • Correct any mismatches in the full registered legal name for the business entity on your Stripe Dashboard, including suffixes such as Ltd, Inc., GmbH, or Pte. Ltd.

Address mismatch or missing

  • Check for missing or mismatched unit, street, city, region, or postal code on the uploaded document vs the Stripe Dashboard.

  • Validate whether Stripe requested for the address of the account representative or the business.

  • Edit the address on your Stripe Dashboard to fully match the submitted document, OR

  • Submit an accepted document type that matches the keyed-in address on your Dashboard.

  • If the country doesn’t have any address verification documents listed or you are missing acceptable documentation, we also accept either:

    • A utility bill issued within the last 6 months
    • A bank statement issued within the last 6 months

  • Refer to our cross border verification requirements page for more details.

Tax or registration ID mismatch

  • For US users: Ensure the legal name entered on your Stripe account matches the TIN in the IRS database, or the legal name on your uploaded document.

  • For non-US users: Check for mismatches between both the tax ID number, and the legal individual/business name associated with it.

  • Correct the business or representative’s ID number on your Stripe Dashboard to reflect a complete match with the IRS database or your document, before uploading the document again.

Wrong document type

  • Ensure that the uploaded document type matches Stripe’s requirements.

  • Re-upload a listed document that’s in Stripe’s acceptable document list, based on account country and the type of verification request.

  • If the country of residence of the Account Representative differs from the country of the Stripe account (that is, country of the business’ legal entity), a passport is required for identity verification.

Unreadable or incomplete file

  • Ensure the uploaded document has no cropping, missing edges or pages, glare, blur, low resolution or non-readable, or a missing reverse side.

  • Ensure an original scan (PDF) or photo (JPEG/PNG) of the document is provided, not a screenshot.

  • Upload a clear original image (JPEG/PNG) or PDF scan. Show the whole document, all four edges, and every required side or page.

    • Photo IDs must be uploaded in color.

Expired or outdated document

  • Expiry date of the document - it must be current and not expired.

  • Any document-age requirements listed on the Stripe Dashboard (for example, issue date within the last 6 months).

  • Upload a current, non-expired accepted document.

Verification requirement remains after submission

  • Whether the review is pending or the Dashboard shows a new error.

  • If the review is pending, wait for 3-5 business days for the outcome rather than repeatedly uploading the same document.

  • If action is required, correct the displayed issue first.

Step 3: Final Checklist

Before uploading a new document, complete this checklist to help ensure your document is accepted.

  • The document is accepted for the account country and exact requirement.
  • Full legal names for individuals match exactly, including middle names and suffixes.
  • Every address component matches.
  • The legal business name, entity type, and tax or registration number match official records.
  • All requested owners, directors, and representatives are included under the correct legal entity.
  • The uploaded document is current, readable, unaltered, and not a screenshot.
  • Upload the complete document in a single file, including all required pages or sides, with all four edges of each page visible. Do not upload pages separately.

Don’t upload the same unchanged document again. Correct the underlying data mismatch, document-type issue, or image-quality problem first.

Troubleshooting secure uploads to the Support site

In some cases, Stripe will require you to provide documentation to verify your identity to help take action on your account. This can be done securely via the Stripe Support site by following the links provided in your support case correspondence; please do not email Stripe with your documentation.

If you are running into issues with uploading your file(s), try the following steps:

GENERAL TROUBLESHOOTING

Please note the below guidelines for uploading your file(s):

  • Only one document can be uploaded per link
  • File size limit – 32 mb
  • File types accepted – .docx, .csv, .xlsx, .pdf, .jpg, .jpeg, .png, .tiff
    • iOS users: If you are trying to upload directly from your phone and your photo is in .heic format, you will need to change the “Camera > Formats” setting to be “Most Compatible” to take a .jpg instead.

GOVERNMENT-ISSUED ID UPLOADS

Make sure that your uploaded photo / ID meet all of these requirements:

  • The photo includes both your ID and a piece of paper that has today’s date written on it
  • The photo is in color and is not blurry, with all information fully visible
  • The photo contains a physical ID with all edges included (scanned/printed copies are not acceptable)
  • Your ID must not be expired
  • Your ID cannot be altered, redacted, or damaged in any way

If you are using your mobile phone, try laying the ID on a flat, contrasting surface in a well-lit room to provide the best possible photo.

Troubleshooting UAE Verification Issues

Overview

If the documents uploaded for verification don’t meet our requirements, you’ll receive an error message from us explaining why the document isn’t acceptable. You can find this verification feedback in two places:

  • On your Dashboard, you’ll see a red banner highlighting that we require more documents/information
  • In a feedback email to the account owner

Why your documents might have been rejected

Trade License/Freelancer Permit

  • The license/permit is expired: if your trade license/permit is expired, we cannot accept it for verification. You must wait until you have the renewed document to continue with the verification process
  • The license/permit is not issued in the UAE: we can only accept licenses/permits that are issued within the UAE for a UAE Stripe account
  • Name mismatch: the business name on your account does not match the business name on the license/permit
  • Emirate mismatch: The emirate in which your license/permit was issued does not match the emirate of your business’s address on your Stripe account
  • Missing representative information: the Stripe account representative is not listed on the trade license/permit

Memorandum of Association

  • Missing ownership information: the document does not include information on the split of ownership of the business. To verify an MoA, the document needs to show all owners of the business and the split of shares between these owners.
  • Name mismatch: the business name does not match the name of the business on the Stripe account
  • Missing owners: owners listed on the MoA are not present as owners on the Stripe account. Any individual who owns 25% or more of the business is required to be added as an owner to your Stripe account. If your business is partially or wholly owned by another business, you’ll need to provide an MoA or equivalent document for that business so we can identify which owners are required to be present on the account. This will require individuals from the holding company to be added to your Stripe account and verified in cases where these individuals ultimately own 25% or more of your business.

Proof of Bank Account

  • Invalid document type: the document is not a valid/official source of proof from your bank. For verification, we require either a scanned copy of a physical letter issued by your bank or an exported PDF statement from your bank’s web portal or app.
    • We cannot accept letters drawn up by anyone other than your bank or screenshots of banking apps.
  • The document is password protected: we can’t review documents that are password protected. Please export the document as a non-password protected PDF or JPEG for review.
  • Incorrect name: the bank account is not in the name of your business. We can only accept personal bank accounts for single member LLCs. If your business is not a single member LLC, you are required to provide proof of a business bank account for verification.

Power of Attorney

  • Missing name: the document does not contain the business name on the Stripe account
  • Missing representative: the document does not contain the name of the company representative on the Stripe account

Passport

  • Incorrect DOB: there is a date of birth mismatch between the document and the Stripe account
  • Name mismatch: the name on the document is different to the name on the Stripe account
  • Missing pages or unreadable: the document uploaded is missing pages (front or back) or is illegible
  • Expired: the passport is expired
  • ID number mismatch: the ID number on the account does not match the ID number on the passport
    • Applies to non-UAE residents

Residency visa

  • Incorrect DOB: date of birth mismatch between the document and the Stripe account
  • Name mismatch: the name on the document is different to the name on the Stripe account
  • Missing pages or unreadable: the document uploaded is missing pages (front or back) or is illegible
  • Expired: the visa is expired

Emirates ID

  • Incorrect DOB: date of birth mismatch between the document and the Stripe account
  • Name mismatch: the name on the document is different to the name on the Stripe account
  • Missing pages or unreadable: the document uploaded is missing pages (front or back) or is illegible
  • Expired: the visa is expired
  • ID number mismatch: the ID number on the account does not match the ID number on the EID
    • Applies to UAE residents

You can correct any of the above information or upload new documents by navigating to Settings > Business Details on the Dashboard

Other FAQs

I’m being asked to add additional owners to my account but they’re not involved with my business?

If we identify an individual who owns 25% or more of your business, they are required to be added as an owner on your Stripe account and verified as an ultimate beneficial owner. This may involve adding individuals from holding companies who are not involved in the running of your business if they ultimately own a 25% or more share of your business.

If we’re requesting owners to be added who have left the company since your documents were drafted, please upload a share sale certificate or amendment to the MoA/AoA that details this change in ownership. You can upload this document via the Dashboard where we request a memorandum of association (by going to Settings > Business details).

Why am I being asked for a power of attorney document? What is a power of attorney document?

We request a power of attorney document if the manager/account representative on the Stripe account is not present on your trade license or memorandum of association. You can find more details about the power of attorney document here: support.stripe.com

Some of the owners of my business are under 13 years old. What do I need to do?

Due to policy restrictions, we can’t support businesses whose owners are minors.

I’m being asked to provide a memorandum of association but my business doesn’t have one?

If your business is a sole establishment, you might have signed up as the incorrect legal entity type. You can change this by going to Settings > Tax details on the Dashboard.

If your business is not a sole establishment, you will need to provide some documentation that outlines the ownership structure of the business.

UAE account activation requirements

To activate a UAE Stripe account, users must upload specific business and identity documents for verification via their Stripe Dashboard. For businesses, this includes trade licenses, memorandums of association, and proof of an active bank account. For individuals, color copies of passports, Emirates IDs, and residence visas are required for company representatives and all owners with 25% or more ownership in the business.

Activating your UAE account

As part of your account setup, we must upload specific business and identity documents for verification.

Documents must be uploaded via your Stripe Dashboard and verified by Stripe before your account can begin to process payments.

To check your account’s outstanding verification requirements:

  • Check your Dashboard for notifications
  • Go to Settings > Business details for more information

See also: Using the API to upload UAE verification documents.

Required Business/Legal Entity Documents

For sole establishments, free zone establishments or branches of sole establishments, we require:

  • Trade license or freelancer permit issued within the UAE

For LLCs, free zone LLCs or branches of LLCs, we require:

  • Trade license or freelancer permit issued within the UAE
  • Memorandum of association (or equivalent document) which shows the beneficial owners of your business and the split of shares between owners
  • Proof of active bank account such as a bank account statement (dated within the last six months)

If any holding companies have 25% or more ownership of your business, you’ll need to upload a memorandum of association or equivalent document for these entities as well. We will continue to request the MoA of nested entities until all individual beneficial owners have been identified.

In addition, if the company representative of your Stripe account is not a named manager or ultimate beneficial owner listed on your trade license or memorandum of association, we must submit a Power of Attorney document for the company representative. This document must be dated within the last three months.

See: Verification of businesses in the UAE.

Required Personal Documents

For the company representative and all individual owners with 25% or more ownership in your business, you must submit a color copy of specific identity documents, as outlined below:

  • Passport, Emirates ID: for UAE nationals or GCC nationals living in the UAE
  • Passport, Emirates ID and Residence Visa: for non-GCC and non-UAE nationals living in the UAE. Residence Visa is optional for Emirates IDs issued on or after April 11, 2022.
  • Passport: for individuals not living in the UAE

Any individual who ultimately owns 25% or more of your business will need to be added as an owner on the Stripe account. This includes individual owners from any holding companies that ultimately own a significant portion of your business (25% or more).

See: Owner verification in the UAE

Document requirements

You may submit:

  • Copies and scans in PDF format or a picture of the original physical document in JPEG or PNG format.
  • Screenshots aren’t acceptable.
  • The format must be no more than one step removed from the original document. Images can’t be processed, converted, or embedded in other files.

Renewing expired documents

We are required to keep up to date with expired documents, including expired trade licenses and identity documents.

See: Continuous Verification in the UAE

UAE business verification requirements

To verify the business opening the Stripe account, we require different documents and information depending on the business type. To check what verification requirements are outstanding on your account, check your Dashboard for notifications or go to Settings > Business details.

Sole establishments, branches of sole establishments and free zone establishments

Requirements:

  • A valid, non-expired trade license or freelancer permit issued within the UAE.
    • We cannot support users who do not have a trade license/permit or whose trade license/permit was issued outside of the UAE.

The only individual person on your Stripe account must be the business owner unless the only individual person listed on the trade license is the business manager - in that case, the manager is required to be the individual on the account.

Examples

  • If your trade license lists a business owner and one or more managers, the business owner must be the individual person added to the account for verification.
  • If your trade license only lists managers (that is, no mention of the business owner), then the manager on the trade license must be the individual person added to the account for verification.

LLCs, branches of LLCs, and free zone LLCs

Requirements:

  • A valid, non-expired, trade license issued within the UAE.
    • We cannot support users who don’t have a trade license or whose trade license was issued outside of the UAE.
  • A memorandum of association (or equivalent document).
  • Proof of active bank account.

The memorandum of association (or equivalent document) must show:

  • The business name.
  • All business owners.
  • The split of shares/ownership between the owners.

UAE Bank Account Verification (BAV)

Acceptable Documents:

  • Bank account statement
    • Bank account must be a Supported banks in the UAE, otherwise it is not supported and will not be able to receive payouts from Stripe
  • Bank letter
    • Document must be dated, and must be issued within the last 6 months
    • Document must contain the bank account owner name and bank account number

The business name required on your documents will depend on your business type and bank account type. See the table below for examples:

Business type

Bank account type

Name requirement

Sole establishment & Free zone establishment

Personal bank account

Owner Name on the Stripe account

Single-Member LLC

Personal bank account, Business bank account

Business Name or Owner Name on the Stripe account

Multi-Member LLC / all other company types

Business bank account

Business Name on the Stripe account

You may also be asked for a power of attorney document if the representative on your Stripe account is not present on the memorandum of association or trade license. This document should indicate that your account representative has been given the power to represent the business on the Stripe account. It must meet the following requirements:

  • Includes the company name.
  • Includes the name of the account representative.
  • Shows confirmation that the representative has been given the power to create a Stripe account on behalf of the business.
  • In PDF format.
  • Dated within the last six months.

Business ownership

As part of the verification process, we’re required to verify the ultimate beneficial owners of your business, which is any individual who owns 25% or more of the business. This may include owners from holding companies if your business is partially or wholly owned by other entities.

If your UAE trade licence lists any managers or executives in addition to the business owner, each of those individuals must also be added to your Stripe account and complete identity verification. This applies regardless of ownership percentage.

Managers listed on your trade licence should be added to your Stripe account under the role of Controller. Adding them as an Owner (without Controller designation) will not satisfy this requirement.

Sole Establishments

The individual person on the account must be the business owner and provide all requested information and documents for verification.

The only exception is for businesses whose trade license or permit only shows the manager of the business (that is, no owners are listed on the trade license or permit). In this case, the manager is required to be the individual listed on the Stripe account.

LLCs

Any individual person who holds 25% or more ownership share of the business must be added to the Stripe account as an owner and provide their documents for verification.

If your business is partially or wholly owned by another legal entity, the individual owners of that business should be added to your Stripe account as owners if they ultimately have a 25% or more ownership share of your business. These owners may not be involved in the operation of your business but are still required to be present on the Stripe account as they are legally beneficial owners.

The memorandum of association (or equivalent document) for all legal entities with 25% or more ownership of your business will need to be uploaded for verification also. This document is required to identify which beneficial owners are required to be present on the Stripe account.

UAE ownership verification requirements

As part of the onboarding process, Stripe is required to verify the identity of any owners and managers added to your account. These individuals are required to provide different documents and information depending on their nationality and place of residence:

UAE or GCC nationals living in the UAE:

  • Passport
  • Emirates ID

Non-UAE or non-GCC nationals living in the UAE:

  • Passport
  • Emirates ID
  • Residence visa (physical page within your passport or digital visa from ICA app)
    • For visas issued after April 11th 2022, we will accept an Emirates ID in place of a residence visa

Individuals residing outside the UAE:

  • Passport

Expired documents are not accepted. If any of the required documents have expired or are in the process of being renewed, you’ll need to wait until you can upload the renewed document to complete verification.

Power of Attorney

If the company representative/manager on your account is not named on the memorandum of association or the trade license as a manager, you’ll be asked to provide a Power of Attorney document. This document should be on company letterhead and serve as proof that the individual currently on the Stripe account has been nominated by the business to open a Stripe account on its behalf.

URL requirements for Stripe India users

In addition to providing a valid business website, Stripe India users are required to submit additional URLs that clearly indicate: their product or service’s terms and conditions, the timelines for processing returns and refunds per the Guidelines on Regulation of Payment Aggregators and Payment Gateways, and their privacy policy.

What URLs are required?

In addition to a valid business website, the following URLs must be provided to activate your account:

  • Terms and Conditions (T&C)
  • Return/Refund/Cancellation policy
  • Privacy policy

Return/Refund/Cancellation policy

The URL must contain information on:

  • Whether the product/service is refundable or cancellable
  • Where applicable conditions to qualify for a refund/return/cancellation, how to initiate the refund/return/cancellation and the timeline for processing the refund/return/cancellation
  • Shipping/delivery policy

US connected accounts accepting card payments verification requirement changes

What specifically is changing?

  • Required information collected from connected accounts. We’re updating the information we require from sole proprietorships, non-profits and single-member LLCs and simplifying how we obtain legal guardian consent for accounts opened by minors. In addition, an email for the account representative is now required for all legal entity types, and a change for government entities and public companies.
  • How we verify business information and provide new detailed verification responses. We’re updating our criteria for valid business information and introducing new verification error codes when we unable to accept or verify information provided.
  • Threshold at which we verify tax identification numbers (TINs). For Custom and Express connected accounts, we’re lowering the payments volume threshold at which we verify TINs to align with current federal tax reporting thresholds.
  • How we prefill statement descriptors and statement descriptor prefixes. If a statement descriptor isn’t provided, the prefill logic has changed to use either the business profile name, the business URL, or the legal entity name of the connected account.

These changes will affect all users with a requested card_payments capability in the US.

Required information collected from connected accounts

New information collected and new fields added to the API:

  • Businesses that are company.structure of sole_proprietorship and single_member_llc, must provide their business address (“company address”). In the event that the business address is the same as the representative’s personal address, your connected accounts can provide the same values for both.
  • Legal entities that are company.structure of government_instrumentality, tax_exempt_government_instrumentality, governmental_unit, public_company, and public_corporation, public_partnership must provide an email for the account representative.This requirement now applies to all legal entity types.
  • To simplify how we obtain a legal guardian’s consent for accounts opened by minors, the Persons API has been updated with a new relationship type of legal_guardian as well as an additional_tos_acceptances field to record the legal guardian’s agreement to the Stripe Terms of Service. If the account representative’s date of birth indicates the individual is a minor, then an account requirement is triggered to add a legal_guardian before the account can be activated.

See the full list of required verification information to collect during onboarding for your specific connected account configurations.

We’ll request the following information from your connected accounts:

Additional considerations

Last four digits required at onboarding for all account types, including Custom and Express connected accounts.

This is the current behavior for Standard connected accounts.

If we can’t programmatically obtain the full nine digit SSN for an individual associated with your account using information already provided, you must provide the full nine digits.

Only applies to non-US resident Reps.
